docs.title: Common Structures
docs.text: Canonical definitions for small, frequently reused data structures across DRS classes. These structs are referenced by multiple classes such as CGeoMesh, CGeoSubset, and CGeoMaterial.

docs.title: Face
docs.text:
A Face represents a triangle defined by three 16-bit vertex indices into a mesh’s vertices array.

Field Type Description i0 ushort Index of first vertex (0-based) i1 ushort Index of second vertex (0-based) i2 ushort Index of third vertex (0-based)

Notes - Each face always references exactly three vertices — only triangles are supported. - The 16-bit limit applies to each stored vertex index, not to the number of triangles. Count fields in the enclosing mesh blocks are separate 32-bit integers.

docs.title: Index Capacity Versus Exporter Limits
docs.text:
Constraint Description 0 ≤ index ≤ 65,535 Range of one unsigned 16-bit index. This can address 65,536 distinct zero-based vertex slots. index < vertex_count Every index must refer to an existing vertex. index_count = face_count * 3 Each triangle consumes three indices; this does not make index_count a 16-bit field. Exporter validation: at most 32,767 vertices A separate implementation check on each render mesh and on the combined welded mesh, not a limit derived from the index field's width.

There is no supported deduction of a 21,845-triangle limit from three ushort indices per face. Reusing vertices allows many triangles to reference the same vertex slots. No additional game-side triangle-count limit has been established here; a wider serialized count is not a guarantee that arbitrarily large meshes work in game.

Sources: Face serialization, mesh definitions, current vertex-count validation.

docs.title: Vertex (Vector4)
docs.text:
A Vertex used by many classes is a 4D float vector where w is always 1.0.

Component Type Description x float X coordinate y float Y coordinate z float Z coordinate w float Always 1.0 (homogeneous coordinate)

Notes - The extra component w exists for alignment and homogeneous transform support. - Importers typically ignore w since it’s constant.

docs.title: Vector3
docs.text:
A 3D point or direction, stored as three 32-bit floats (x, y, z). Total size: 12 bytes.

Component Type Bytes Notes x float 4 little-endian IEEE-754 y float 4 z float 4

Usage Common across geometry and animation data (e.g., CGeoAABox, marker positions/directions, etc.).

Constraints / Conventions - Exactly 3 floats; no padding or w component. - Coordinate meaning depends on the parent structure (position vs. direction).

docs.title: Matrix3x3
docs.text:
A 3×3 linear basis stored as 9 floats in row-major order. Its interpretation depends on the consuming block; it is not universally a unit-length rotation matrix. Total size: 36 bytes.

Row Elements Type Bytes 0 m00 m01 m02 float 12 1 m10 m11 m12 float 12 2 m20 m21 m22 float 12

Usage Represents orientation in CMatCoordinateSystem and other transforms. Stored/serialized as 9 consecutive floats.

Constraints / Conventions - Check the consuming block before normalizing the basis. OBB nodes deliberately include box size in the matrix; normalizing those vectors would discard the dimensions. - Scale behavior for other block types is not established by the shared storage layout alone. Preserve imported values rather than assuming either universal scale support or a universal prohibition. - Serialization is strictly 9 floats; no implicit translation.

docs.title: Matrix4x4
docs.text:
A full 4×4 transform matrix stored as 16 floats in row-major order. Total size: 64 bytes.

Row Elements Type Bytes 0 m00 m01 m02 m03 float 16 1 m10 m11 m12 m13 float 16 2 m20 m21 m22 m23 float 16 3 m30 m31 m32 m33 float 16

Usage Used where a complete affine transform is required (e.g., skeleton super-parent). Written row by row.

Constraints / Conventions - 16 floats, no extra padding. - Meaning of the last column/row follows typical affine layout; specific interpretation depends on the consuming block.

docs.title: CMatCoordinateSystem
docs.text:
Compact transform pairing a linear basis (Matrix3x3) with position (Vector3). Total size: 48 bytes (36 + 12).

Field Type Bytes Description matrix Matrix3x3 36 Block-specific linear basis (row-major) position Vector3 12 Translation (x, y, z)

Usage - Core transform used by many blocks: SLocator, OBBNode, BoxShape, CylinderShape, SphereShape, etc. - Always serialized as 9 floats (matrix) followed by 3 floats (position).

Constraints / Conventions - There is no separate scale field, but the 3×3 matrix can encode scale. For OBB nodes, the exporter explicitly multiplies axes by their half-extents before serialization. - Whether another consumer accepts scaled bases is a separate engine question; it remains unverified here for locators and collision primitives. Do not infer that any arbitrary Blender transform is supported in every block. - See the OBB notes and the OBB exporter before interpreting axis lengths or changing normalization.

docs.title: CSkSkeleton
docs.text: Stores the bone hierarchy (skeleton) used for animating skinned meshes. It defines the names, parent-child relationships, and bind-pose transformations for all bones. 🦴

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Purpose: Defines the articulated structure (bones) that drives the deformation of animated characters and objects.
  • Where it appears: Included in animated model types: AnimatedUnit, AnimatedObjectNoCollision, AnimatedObjectCollision. It's absent in static models. Appears after CSkSkinInfo in the WriteOrder.
  • Engine impact: Forms the basis for skeletal animation playback. The number of bones and hierarchy depth can affect animation performance.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: Field Type Description magic int32 Internal block identifier, should be 1558308612. version int32 Format version, typically 3. bone_matrix_count int32 Number of entries in bone_matrices. Should match bone_count. bone_matrices List[BoneMatrix] Bind pose transformation data for each bone, ordered sequentially by bone identifier (0, 1, 2...). See BoneMatrix. bone_count int32 Total number of bones in the skeleton. bones List[Bone] The list defining each bone's properties and hierarchy. Note: This list is ordered by Bone.version, not necessarily by bone identifier. See Bone. super_parent Matrix4x4 Root transformation matrix, usually identity. See Matrix4x4.

docs.title: BoneMatrix
docs.text:
Contains bind pose data derived from four BoneVertex entries, effectively storing the bone's local transform relative to its parent (or world space for root bones).

Field Type Description bone_vertices List[BoneVertex] Four vertices defining the bone's orientation, position, and hierarchical links. Always 4 entries. See BoneVertex.

docs.title: BoneVertex
docs.text:
A helper structure within BoneMatrix. The parent field is key for linking within the skeleton's structure, particularly for the first two vertices.

Field Type Description position Vector3 A 3D coordinate related to the bone's bind pose. See Vector3. parent int32 Index linking to bone identifiers, with specific meaning based on its index within bone_vertices:

Specific parent field usage within BoneMatrix.bone_vertices:

  • bone_vertices[0].parent: Stores the identifier of this bone's parent bone in the hierarchy. For the root bone (identifier 0), this value is -1. This directly links a bone back to its parent.
  • bone_vertices[1].parent: Stores the identifier of the bone itself. This acts as a self-reference.
  • bone_vertices[2].parent: Hardcoded to 0 during export (create_skeleton). Its specific use in-game is unclear.
  • bone_vertices[3].parent: Hardcoded to 0 during export (create_skeleton). Its specific use in-game is unclear.

docs.title: Bone
docs.text:
Defines a single bone in the skeleton hierarchy. Remember this list is ordered by version, not identifier.

Field Type Description version uint32 Bone version/identifier, often derived from a hash or predefined list (bone_versions.json). Used for sorting this list. identifier int32 Unique ID for this bone within the skeleton (0 for root, 1, 2...). Used by CSkSkinInfo and CDspJointMap. Used for indexing bone_matrices. name_length int32 Length of the bone name string. name string Name of the bone (e.g., "Bip01_Head"). Limited to 63 characters by importer/exporter (hashes longer names). child_count int32 Number of direct children this bone has. children List[int32] List of identifier values for the children bones.

docs.title: Authoring & In-Game Behavior
docs.text:
• Blender Workflow:
    • Creation: Created automatically during export (create_skeleton in drs_utility.py) from a Blender Armature object within the model's collection.
    • Hierarchy: The parent-child relationships in the Blender Armature directly define the Bone.children and the BoneVertex[0].parent links in the exported CSkSkeleton. The root bone in Blender (usually the one with no parent) becomes bone identifier 0.
    • Bone Map: The exporter generates a bone_map (create_bone_map) which assigns a unique sequential identifier (0, 1, 2...) to each bone based on traversing the hierarchy. This map is crucial for linking skin weights (CSkSkinInfo) and joint maps (CDspJointMap), and determines the order of the bone_matrices array.
    • Bone Ordering: The bones list itself is sorted based on the Bone.version field (potentially from bone_versions.json or a hash) before writing. The bone_matrices list remains ordered by the hierarchical identifier.
    • Naming: Bone names are taken directly from the Blender Armature. The importer/exporter enforces a 63-character limit; longer names might be hashed (Bone.read logic). Standard naming conventions (like "Bip01_...") are recommended.
    • Bind Pose: The bone_matrices are calculated from the bone's Rest Pose transforms in Blender (armature_bone.matrix_local).
  • Import: When importing (import_csk_skeleton, init_bones), the CSkSkeleton data is used to reconstruct the Armature object in Blender, including bone names, hierarchy (create_bone_tree uses parent links), and setting the Rest Pose (record_bind_pose).

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text: Rule Why magic == 1558308612 Confirms block type. version == 3 Ensures expected format. bone_matrix_count == bone_count Each bone needs matrix data. bone_count == len(bones) Bone array must match its count. Bone identifier values are unique and sequential (0 to bone_count-1) Required for consistent indexing by other systems. Child indices in Bone.children are valid bone identifier values Prevents broken hierarchy links. BoneVertex[0].parent index is valid (-1 or 0 to bone_count-1) Ensures correct parent linking. BoneVertex[1].parent == Bone.identifier Consistency check for self-reference. Bone names are unique and <= 63 chars Ensures correct mapping and avoids engine/tool limitations.

docs.title: Cross-References
docs.text:
• Header / Nodes: Referenced via NodeInformation in the DRS header. See Header.
  • Skinning Weights: Provides the bone identifier values referenced by CSkSkinInfo. See CSkSkinInfo.
  • Joint Map: Provides the bone identifier values referenced by CDspJointMap. See CDspJointMap.
  • Common Structures: Uses Matrix4x4 and Vector3. See Common Structures.

docs.title: Nice to know
docs.text:
• Magic Value: CSkSkeleton = -2110567991 (0x823299C9). See Glossary → MagicValues.
  • Node Name: The node is typically named csk_skeleton in the hierarchy during export.
  • Ordering Difference: Be aware that the bones list is sorted by version, while bone_matrices are indexed by the sequential identifier. This means bones[i].identifier does not necessarily equal i.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
CSkSkinInfo defines how each vertex in a mesh is influenced by bones from the skeleton. It determines how meshes deform when animated. Each vertex stores a small list of bones and their respective weights. This block appears in animated DRS assets and is generated automatically when the model has an armature with vertex groups.

In the WriteOrder defined in drs_definitions.py, it appears for: - AnimatedUnit - AnimatedObjectCollision - AnimatedObjectNoCollision

It is not used for static objects without a skeleton.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: Field Type Description version int32 Internal version number for the format. vertex_count int32 Number of vertices with weight data. vertex_data List[VertexData] One entry per vertex, containing bone indices and weights.

docs.title: VertexData
docs.text: Field Type Description bone_indices List[int] Bone IDs influencing this vertex. The IDs reference the bones from CSkSkeleton. weights List[float] Normalized influence weights for each bone index (usually up to 4 per vertex).

docs.title: Authoring & In-Game Behavior
docs.text:
When exporting from Blender, the create_skin_info() function in drs_utility.py gathers the skin data like this:

  1. Vertex Source: A unified list of all mesh vertices is created (from the exported mesh). Vertices are matched by position using rounding and KD-tree lookup to ensure each Blender vertex connects to the correct exported vertex.

  2. Bone Mapping: Blender’s vertex groups are matched to bones in the armature. The mapping uses the bone names from CSkSkeleton to find the correct bone ID. Each vertex group name must exactly match its bone name to export correctly.

  3. Weight Handling: Each vertex can store up to 4 influences. If more are found, only the 4 highest weights are kept. Weights are then normalized to ensure their total equals 1.0.

  4. Import Behavior: When importing, the tool recreates vertex groups in Blender based on stored bone indices and weights, matching the bones from the linked skeleton. Missing bones or mismatched names are skipped but logged for visibility.

In-game, this data ensures that mesh vertices follow the correct bones as they animate. Missing or invalid weights can cause visible stretching or collapsing of the model.

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text: Rule Why it matters Each vertex has ≤ 4 influences Game engine expects a fixed small number for performance. Weights per vertex sum to 1.0 Prevents visual deformation errors. Each bone index exists in CSkSkeleton Ensures valid bone links for animation. Vertex match succeeds during export Prevents missing weight assignments.

docs.title: Cross-References
docs.text:
• Skeleton: CSkSkeleton — provides the bone hierarchy and IDs used here.
  • Mesh: CDspMeshFile — contains the vertices that the weights are applied to.
  • Joint Mapping: CDspJointMap — connects mesh joints to the correct bones.
  • Write Order: Listed for animated objects in drs_definitions.py.

docs.title: Nice to know
docs.text:
• This block is written only when a mesh has vertex groups and a valid armature.
  • If bone names don’t match exactly between Blender and the skeleton, those weights are skipped and logged.
  • Removing unused vertex groups before export helps reduce unnecessary data and warnings.

docs.title: DrwResourceMeta
docs.text: Contains metadata about the DRS resource, specifically a version number and a hash string.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Purpose: Stores basic metadata, primarily a hash likely used for asset identification or version tracking.
  • Where it appears: Present in all defined model types (AnimatedUnit, StaticObjectCollision, StaticObjectNoCollision, AnimatedObjectNoCollision, AnimatedObjectCollision). See WriteOrder.
  • Engine impact: Likely used by the engine or tools for identifying or verifying the asset version. It doesn't directly affect rendering or gameplay mechanics visible to artists.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: Field Type Description version int32 Format version number, typically 1. unknown int32 An unknown integer value. Observed values include 0, 1, 2, 3. Default appears to be 1 for units. length int32 Length of the following hash string in bytes. hash string A string containing hash information (e.g., "sr-1234567890-0").

docs.title: Authoring & In-Game Behavior
docs.text:
• Blender Workflow: This block is generated automatically by the exporter (save_drs calls DrwResourceMeta().write). Artists do not directly edit this data in Blender.
  • Hash Generation: The exporter currently generates a default hash string (""). The specific logic for generating meaningful hashes (like "sr-crc32-0") might reside elsewhere or in older toolchains. The importer (DrwResourceMeta().read) simply reads the existing hash from the file.
  • unknown field: The purpose of this field is unclear.

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text: Rule Why version == 1 Confirms expected format. length matches actual hash string length Prevents reading incorrect data or buffer overflows.

docs.title: Cross-References
docs.text:
• Header / Nodes: Referenced via NodeInformation in the DRS header. See Header.
  • Glossary: Contains the magic value. See Glossary → MagicValues.

docs.title: Nice to know
docs.text:
• Magic Value: DrwResourceMeta = -183033339 (0xF518F885).
  • Although present in all models, the actual meaning or usage of the hash string by the game engine isn't known. It likely serves as a unique identifier or checksum.

docs.title: DRS Header & Core Nodes
docs.text: This section describes the DRS file header and the core node structures on which all class data depends. These structures form the backbone of the DRS archive layout.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Text Only
flowchart TD
  A[DRS Header] --> B[NodeInformation[]]
  A --> C[Node[]]
  B -->|info_index| C
  C -->|name / identifier| D[Class Data Blocks]

Root Elements

  • The first NodeInformation entry and the first Node always represent the Root Node.
  • The Root Node itself does not contain payload data — it only anchors the hierarchy.

docs.title: Header Structure
docs.text:
Field Type Description magic int Constant signature value -981667554 number_of_models uint Always 1 in BattleForge node_information_offset uint Offset where the NodeInformation section starts node_hierarchy_offset uint Offset where the Node section starts node_count uint Total number of Nodes

The first NodeInformation and Node entries at these offsets correspond to the Root Node.

docs.title: RootNodeInformation
docs.text:
Represents metadata for the Root Node and tracks how many additional nodes exist.

Field Type Default Description zeroes[16] int[16] 0 Spacer / padding (16×0) neg_one int -1 Unknown use, always -1 one uint 1 Unknown use, always 1 node_information_count uint – Number of additional NodeInformation entries zero uint 0 Unknown use, always 0

Tip

node_information_count equals node_count - 1, because the Root Node itself is excluded.

docs.title: NodeInformation
docs.text:
Links each Node to the data blob of its class.

Field Type Description magic int Unique magic number identifying the class type identifier uint References Node.info_index (-1 for Root) offset uint File offset where the class data starts size uint Size of the data blob in bytes unused[4] uint[4] Four unused values (ignored in BattleForge / Skylords, used in SpellForce 2)

docs.title: Root Node (first entry in Node hierarchy)
docs.text:
Field Type Default Description identifier uint 0 Identifier of the Root Node unknown uint 0 Unknown, always zero length uint 9 Length of the string "root_node" name str "root_node" Name of the Root Node

The Root Node always has identifier 0 and name "root_node". It precedes all other class nodes in the hierarchy.

docs.title: Node (generic hierarchy entry)
docs.text:
Each Node represents a link between a class name and its corresponding NodeInformation entry. Every Node ends with a zero integer used as a spacer.

Field Type Description info_index uint Index into the NodeInformation table (-1 for Root) length uint Length of the class name string name str The class name zero uint Always 0 (spacer)

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text: Rule Description Header.magic == -981667554 Validates file signature Header.node_count >= 1 At least one node (Root) must exist RootNode.identifier == 0 and RootNode.name == "root_node" Root node consistency len(NodeInformation) == Header.node_count - 1 Node counts must match (-1 for RootNodeInformation) Each Node.info_index >= 0 Must reference valid NodeInformation (except Root) No overlapping offset/size pairs Class data blocks must not overlap

docs.title: Known Variants
docs.text: Game / Version Notes BattleForge / Skylords Reborn unused[4] fields are unused; number_of_models is always 1. SpellForce 2 DRS unused[4] were used to override settings for certain assets.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The DRS Header defines where all structural blocks of the archive begin. From there, each NodeInformation and Node entry establishes the relationship between class metadata and data payloads. Understanding this hierarchy is essential before parsing any of the 15 class structures that follow.

docs.title: Advanced Abilities Guide
docs.text:
Configure attack, casting, and channeling animation metadata after completing the Unit Creation Guide. For timed audio and visual resources, use the Advanced Effects Guide; for attachment points, use the Advanced Locators Guide.

Scope: an entry called an “Ability” in this editor maps a visual job to an animation. It does not create a gameplay ability, projectile behavior, damage, targeting rules, cooldown, or resource cost. Those must already be configured in the game's data. The workflows below concern DRS export; BMG animation/effect export is incomplete and is not an equivalent route.

docs.title: 1. Know Which Data You Are Editing
docs.text:
Data What it contains Where it is authored Blender Action / .ska Bone motion and clip timing Action Editor; Clip Timing... for timing metadata AnimationSet Visual job (vis_job), mode, weighted Action variants, clip segments, markers AnimationSet Editor AnimationTimings Timing category/tag, variant index, millisecond timings, direction, marker reference Generated through the editor's per-variant Timing section EffectSet Audio/FX references scheduled against a named SKA clip EffectSet panel Locators Model or bone attachment points CDrwLocatorList Editor

An animation marker, a locator, and an EffectSet keyframe are separate records. Matching their time or position does not automatically link them or create an in-game event.

docs.title: Templates Are Not Universal Requirements
docs.text:
Init populates the catalog's base template: Idle, Walk, Run, Spawn, HitFromBack, Cheer / Emote, HitFromFront, Die, HitFromLeft, HitFromRight, and PushBackStandUp (Start/Loop/End). This is a useful starting point for many units, not an exporter-enforced checklist for every model. Choose mappings required by the existing unit/game configuration; do not add empty entries just to match this list.

An animated prop may need only Idle. The Animated Object DRS export types retain only visual job 0 (Idle) and remove animation markers and timings. Use Animated Unit when the exported model needs attack/cast mappings and their timing data.

Sources: ability catalog, editor initialization, DRS model-type filtering.

docs.title: 2. Work Safely in the AnimationSet Editor
docs.text:
Make the intended DRSModel_* root collection active, then open 3D Viewport → Sidebar → DRS Editor → AnimationSet Editor. When switching between models, save the current model's edits first and use Reset to load the newly active model's stored data.

Control Actual behavior Init Clears the current editor list, then creates the base template. It is not a harmless refresh. Remove All Clears the working list. Save afterward only if that removal is intended. Save Writes working state to the active collection's AnimationSetJSON; does not export files or save the .blend. Reset Reloads the active collection's stored data, discarding unsaved editor changes. Mode Filters entries by mode. Labels include Base, Special, Rest, and Rest->Base when present. Add Ability… Adds catalog components in the current mode; existing (vis_job, mode) pairs are not added twice. Ability-row minus button Removes that mode-key entry. Grouped rows should be checked carefully after removal. Variant + / − Adds/removes variants of the selected entry.

Save a backup before editing imported metadata: the editor reconstructs its supported schema, not every possible unknown field in an original file.

Source: editor controls and persistence.

docs.title: 3. Choose an Existing Visual Mapping
docs.text:
Use the catalog label matching the model's existing game-side behavior. These are actual catalog entries, not new gameplay ability definitions:

Catalog label Visual-job components Timing category / tag Attack MeleeAttack (8); catalog describes it as melee or ranged Melee / 0; marker required by the catalog Special Melee Attack Ground SpecialMeleeAttack (15) Melee / 114; marker required Special Melee Attack Air SpecialMeleeAttackAir (16) Melee / 115; marker required Cast (Ground Only) CastGround (18), CastResolve (19) CastResolve / 0 Cast (Ground & Air) Ground 18/19, Air 22/21 CastResolve / 0; catalog requires identical ground/air timings PreparedSalvo Ground 185/186, Air 187/188 CastResolve / 54 SpecialRangedAir Cast 316, Resolve 317 CastResolve / 148 Harpoon Cast 321, Resolve 322 CastResolve / 150 Heal Channel Start 177, Loop 178, End 179 Channel / 48

There is no generic catalog entry named Ranged Attack. A regular ranged model can use the existing Attack visual job; a specialized model may use one of the named cast/resolve mappings. The timing label Melee on Attack is not a gameplay switch that makes an attack melee.

Ground-only and ground/air cast entries share visual-job IDs, so they are not independent sets of interchangeable slots. Display labels are inferred from the catalog's ID map and can resolve to the shared ground/air label after reloading.

Mode switching is not a supported recipe. The catalog explicitly calls its entry ModeSwitch (Not yet Supported). SwitchToSpecial and SwitchToNormal are internal component roles sharing job 7, not independent supported animation types. Although ModeSwitch exists in the timing-category enum, that alone does not implement a complete transition workflow. Preserve known working data rather than treating the presence of a label as proof of support.

Sources: catalog labels, IDs and tags, timing-category enum, ID-based grouping.

docs.title: 4. Assign and Check Every Variant
docs.text:
1. Add the matching catalog entry in the intended mode.
  2. Select a variant and choose its Action. The dropdown includes Actions from the entire .blend, not only the current model. Its shortened display label is not necessarily its datablock name or exported filename.
  3. Give each intended variant a weight. 80 and 20 is a useful two-variant convention. Animation weights are individually limited to 0..100 in this UI, but the editor does not normalize their sum or reject totals other than 100. Do not assume a particular engine selection algorithm from the percentage display alone.
  4. Review Allows IK and Force No Blend. New variants default to enabled and disabled respectively; they are metadata flags, not Blender rigging or baking commands. Keep established imported settings unless a deliberate change is needed.
  5. Preview each variant. Play uses the selected variant, not a weighted random sample.

A variant with <None>/an empty Action is skipped when constructing the exported AnimationSet. Merely creating an Action or NLA strip does not add it to an ability mapping.

Sources: variant properties and UI, variant export filtering.

docs.title: 5. Place Markers and Understand Time Units
docs.text:
The catalog enables the Marker section for Spawn, Attack, and selected special mappings. Casting entries normally use Cast→Resolve instead; a marker section is not available for every ability.

Control Meaning in the current editor Time Fraction of the full Action, 0..1; not seconds or a Blender frame number Is Spawn Animation Stored marker flag; seeded for Spawn, not a general gameplay activation toggle Position Stored XYZ event position; choose it against the pose at the marker time Direction Stored direction vector; also orients the display arrow Play Marker Plays from the Action's start to the normalized marker time Display Marker Assigns the Action, jumps to the marker pose, and shows its arrow in DRSMarkers

For a five-second clip, marker 0.6 is at three seconds. To place an event at 0.6 seconds in that clip, use 0.12. EffectSet keyframe times use the same normalized 0..1 convention, so matching fractions aligns the scheduled moments only when both refer to the same full clip.

Keep these editor units separate from unverified game-tick behavior. Historical notes about 100-ms quantization, a 200-ms Spawn minimum, a six-entry limit, and resolve-phase duration are research hypotheses, not confirmed authoring rules. See AnimationTimings research status before interpreting exported millisecond fields.

For a weapon or hand event, inspect the pose with Display Marker, then edit the marker's numeric Position/Direction. Markers are not bone-bound locators, and dragging the helper arrow is not a supported “sync back” workflow: the stored UI values remain authoritative. A marker can be near a projectile attachment point, but neither creates nor automatically links that locator. Retain imported armature/locator parenting; do not reparent bones or locators just to match the helper arrow.

docs.title: Generated Millisecond Timings
docs.text:
The Timing section shows read-only Type, Tag ID, Is Enter Mode, VariantIndex, Cast (ms), Duration (ms), Used FPS, and MarkerID; its Direction remains editable. Change clip timing and the normalized marker/split controls rather than attempting to type new millisecond values.

For timing recomputation, the editor uses the Action's frame_length and original_fps when available, otherwise its frame-range span and effective scene FPS (fps / fps_base). In this implementation:

  • Duration (ms) / exported resolve_ms is the full clip duration.
  • Exported cast_ms is that duration multiplied by marker Time, or by Cast→Resolve when no marker is present.

These are the add-on's calculations, not proof that a specific game-side damage/projectile event uses either field in a particular way. Some older format documentation describes different meanings and editable timing fields; the current editor code is authoritative for these controls.

Sources: marker controls and timing display, timing recomputation, timing serialization, binary marker fields.

docs.title: Cast or Ranged Release Example
docs.text:
1. Use the existing model's mapping: for example Attack for its regular attack or Cast (Ground Only) for an existing generic cast hook.
  2. Assign the full clip, including preparation and follow-through.
  3. For Attack, set marker Time at the visual release/contact pose. For a cast pair, set Cast→Resolve at the transition you want to inspect.
  4. Use Play Cast and Play Resolve to inspect the two ranges of the selected full Action. Resolve rows are hidden in the main ability list.
  5. Configure the required locator separately, then add audio/FX keyframes to the corresponding clip in EffectSet.
  6. Save, export, and test in the game configuration that actually invokes this visual job. A plausible preview does not create a functioning spell or projectile.

Action selection is propagated between corresponding Cast/Resolve entries. Ground and air channels are separate; explicitly verify their clips and matching timings rather than assuming one edit updates both.

docs.title: Loop Set Example
docs.text:
For PushBackStandUp, Heal Channel, or another catalog Start/Loop/End group, the UI shows one Loop Set row. Use a full clip with a preparation, repeatable middle, and exit. Set Start.end and Loop.end, then inspect the Start, Loop, and End preview buttons. Selecting an Action propagates the same variant index's file across the group.

Range caveat: linked Action selection and preview buttons are not a guarantee that every hidden component's exported Start/End values have been synchronized. Current drawing logic updates only the first Start/Loop variants' ranges, and cast previews compute their Resolve range separately. Reimport and check the exported component ranges, especially End/Resolve and additional variants, before relying on segmented playback.

Sources: cast and loop previews, linked Action assignment.

docs.title: 7. Prepare the Actual Export Action
docs.text:
A control rig is an authoring aid; the deform/game armature supplies the exported skeleton and motion. The preview helpers can prefer an armature named Control_Rig, while the SKA exporter explicitly excludes armatures containing that name. Successful control-rig playback therefore does not prove that the export Action contains usable deform-bone motion.

The SKA writer reads the selected Action's bone location and quaternion rotation F-curves. It does not bake evaluated IK/constraints, the NLA stack, Euler rotation, or scale into motion automatically. Bake/convert the intended final motion onto the deform armature's bones before export when the source relies on those systems. Preserve the existing skeleton/rest-pose relationships and bone names; the writer derives bone IDs from known names or its fallback name hash.

Prefer zero-based clip keyframes for new work: SKA sample times are calculated from absolute keyframe numbers divided by clip length, without subtracting an arbitrary Action start offset. A clip moved to a later timeline position can preview correctly yet export shifted times.

Use Clip Timing... to inspect or set per-Action FPS/duration metadata. The dialog offers fixed-frame FPS retiming, duration-to-FPS calculation, FPS/duration-to-frame-length calculation, and scene fallback. These operations set timing metadata; they do not rescale or bake the Action's F-curves. Imported frame_length, original_fps, and original_duration can override later scene changes, so review them after changing a clip's length. Preview can also change scene FPS and timeline limits.

Sources: preview armature lookup, export armature lookup, SKA writer, Clip Timing dialog.

docs.title: SKA Metadata Is Not an AnimationSet Mode
docs.text:
The full track/keyframe path in the current SKA reader/writer is implemented for file types 6 and 7. New SKA exports are generated as type 7; a research template describing types 2–5 does not establish equivalent add-on support for them.

  • Track headers distinguish position (0) from quaternion rotation (1) and bind tracks to skeleton bone IDs. Renaming a clip does not retarget its skeleton.
  • Each keyframe stores four values and four tangent components. This layout is not a generic export path for arbitrary Blender scale, Euler, or constraint animation.
  • Both supported layouts store duration, repeat/stutter metadata, frame length, and trailing integers; type 7 includes an extra integer before frame length. Do not assign guessed meanings to unknown fields. This is not a lossless byte-for-byte rewrite: the current exporter generates three trailing zeros, so keep the original clip as a reference.
  • The writer uses the Action's repeat value when present, otherwise 0, and its stutter_mode when present, otherwise 2. These file-level settings are distinct from AnimationSet's Start/Loop/End clip ranges.
  • Historical notes call frame length “unused” or describe particular stutter values as smooth. Those engine effects remain unverified. The add-on still uses frame-length/FPS metadata for timing calculations; do not discard it or treat it as a guaranteed in-game speed control. Use Clip Timing... and round-trip the result.

docs.title: 8. Save, Export, and Round-Trip Check
docs.text:
1. Inspect every mapping/variant and its timing section, then click Save in both AnimationSet and EffectSet. Save the .blend too.
  2. Export a DRS as Animated Unit for these unit visual mappings.
  3. Enable Export All SKA Actions when new SKA files are needed. Despite its name, this exports clips referenced in the saved AnimationSet blob, not every Action in the file. An EffectSet-only Action reference does not by itself schedule an SKA export. Unresolved Actions can be skipped.
  4. Choose Model Name Prefix deliberately: No Prefix, Model Name Prefix, Folder Name Prefix, or Keep Existing Prefix. The DRS dialog currently defaults to No Prefix, not Model Name Prefix. The naming map rewrites AnimationSet, marker-set and EffectSet animation references together, replacing spaces and resolving filename collisions; check actual output names rather than predicting them from dropdown labels.
  5. For smooth keyed motion, review [DEBUG] Export SKA Tangents (enabled by default in DRS export). The standalone SKA exporter selects one Action and has its own Export Tangents toggle, defaulting to off. Tangents cannot recover missing/baked-out motion.
  6. Reimport the output into a clean test scene and compare clips, mapping IDs, variants, ranges, timing values, marker position/direction, and effects against the source. Finally verify the game-side behavior with its existing ability definitions.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Checklist
docs.text:
Symptom Check first No attack/cast mappings after export Animated Unit type, correct active root, editor Save, nonempty Action assignments; Animated Object intentionally filters these out. Missing or incorrect SKA Saved AnimationSet references, actual Action names, output prefix, ambiguous/truncated names, and exported files. The resolver can fall back to similar prefixes. Motion works only on the control rig Bake deform-bone location/quaternion channels; the writer does not export the evaluated rig/NLA result. Wrong speed or shifted release Per-Action timing metadata, effective FPS, zero-based keyframes, normalized Time versus seconds, and full-clip versus segment timing. Loop/resolve replays the wrong part Reimport and inspect all hidden component ranges and variant indices; preview splits alone are insufficient. Marker display is right but game event is wrong Compare exported marker IDs to AnimationTimings references and confirm the game actually invokes the intended job/tag. Marker-set IDs are regenerated on Save separately from timing IDs; do not assume those links round-trip unchanged. Existing data changes after Save Work on a copy; schema reconstruction is not lossless preservation of unknown fields or unsupported mappings.

Sources: referenced-only SKA export, export naming, DRS export options, Action resolver, marker/timing serialization.

docs.title: Related Reading
docs.text:
• Advanced Effects Guide: audio/FX configuration and preservation caveats.
  • Advanced Locators Guide: attachment types and bone relationships.
  • Unit Creation Guide: shared unit setup, without repeating it here.
  • AnimationSet format and AnimationTimings format: binary structure references; consult the source links above for current UI behavior.

docs.title: Advanced Effects Guide
docs.text:
Use EffectSet to schedule existing sound and visual-effect resources against skeletal animation clips. Complete the Unit Creation Guide first; use the Advanced Abilities Guide for Action mappings, markers, and cast/loop segmentation.

Scope: this editor authors timed resource references in a DRS, not particle systems, sound files, projectile simulation, or gameplay abilities. It does not establish damage, cooldowns, targeting, or spell behavior. The BMG export path has unfinished animation/effect nodes; do not assume it exports the configuration described here.

Back up imported models before pressing Save. The current EffectSet UI exposes only animation-keyed entries. Its Save operation rebuilds that subset and does not preserve imported impact/additional sound containers or all header/unknown data. See round-trip limitations before editing a working game asset.

docs.title: 1. Understand the Three Levels
docs.text:
Level Contents Example authoring intent Effect entry An Action / .ska reference plus keyframes Events for the clip used by an existing Attack mapping Keyframe Normalized time, type, audio/spatial parameters, resource variants A sound at the release pose Variant File reference and weight Two alternative existing sounds for that one event

These variants are independent of AnimationSet variants. One chooses a motion clip; the other supplies candidate resources for a scheduled event. If Attack has two different SKA clips, create/check an EffectSet entry for each clip that needs events. There is no automatic “apply this effect to every Attack variant” link.

An entry is keyed by the animation filename, not an ability label, Blender timeline marker, or locator name. Several visual jobs can refer to the same clip; EffectSet does not provide a separate per-ability selector for them.

Sources: EffectSet editor state, binary Keyframe and SkelEff definitions.

docs.title: 2. Open the Correct Model's Data
docs.text:
Make the intended DRSModel_* root collection active and open 3D Viewport → Sidebar → DRS Editor → EffectSet. The panel remains visible without a valid root, but shows a selection hint instead of data controls. Save pending edits before changing models, then use Reset to load the newly active root's stored state.

  • Save: writes the working EffectSet state into the collection's EffectSetJSON property. It does not save the .blend, export the DRS, or write/copy resource files.
  • Reset: reloads stored EffectSet data and discards unsaved panel changes.
  • Left-list + / −: add/remove an Effect entry.
  • Action: choose the animation associated with that entry. The dropdown draws from all Actions in the .blend; check that it belongs to the intended skeleton/model.
  • Keyframes + / −: add/remove scheduled events. A newly added keyframe starts at 0, defaults to FX1, and includes one empty resource variant.
  • Up/down arrows: reorder keyframe records, not their time values. The editor does not automatically sort by Time.
  • Variants + / −: add/remove candidates for the selected event; edit File and Weight below the list.

The Action label can be shortened for display; it is not a reliable preview of the exported filename. Imported entries also retain their original SKA name internally. See the Action-retargeting caveat below before changing an imported entry's dropdown.

Sources: panel controls, add/save/reset operators.

docs.title: 3. Select the Event Type and Resource
docs.text:
Type shown in the UI Stored value Resource category Audio (snr/wav) 0 Existing .snr or .wav sound reference FX1 (fxb) 1 Existing .fxb visual-effect reference FX2 (fxb) 2 Existing .fxb visual-effect reference Permanent FX1 (fxb) 3 Permanent-effect category, referencing an .fxb Permanent FX2 (fxb) 4 Permanent-effect category, referencing an .fxb

These keyframe types are separate from the type field in the format's additional sound containers. Research labels such as StepSound refer to that other structure, not to a selectable replacement for keyframe type 0. The current panel does not author those containers; see round-trip limitations.

The labels establish supported categories, not a complete explanation of the engine difference between FX1 and FX2 or permanent-effect lifetime/cleanup. Reuse a known working model's type when reproducing an existing effect. Do not infer that type 3 or 4 means a Blender loop or that the add-on simulates its persistence.

docs.title: File References and Paths
docs.text:
The File (.fxb/.wav/.snr) field is a plain string. Enter the resource reference expected by the game's content layout, following a comparable working asset's naming/path convention. For illustration, example_attack.wav or example_release.fxb are filenames only, not bundled resources or guaranteed game-valid assets.

  • EffectSet export stores the resource string; it does not validate existence, enforce an extension, convert audio, or package the referenced resource.
  • A local Windows path used while editing is not automatically rewritten into a deployable game-resource path. Do not leave an absolute workstation path unless the target workflow explicitly supports it.
  • Preserve the spelling and relative subpath used by known working content. Confirm the files are installed where the game resolves those references.
  • Keep animation .ska references separate from sound/FX File fields. The exporter's shared SKA naming map updates animation references, not the names of external .fxb/.wav/.snr resources.
  • Export skips empty resource names. Fill at least one intended resource variant per event and remove empty test events rather than assuming they will produce useful output.

Sources: type/file properties, resource serialization, shared SKA naming.

docs.title: SNR/SNS Resources and Sound Registration
docs.text:
An .snr is not simply a WAV file with a different extension. EA AudioCore v0 headers describe the codec, channel configuration, sample rate, sample count, and loop metadata. Depending on the storage type, audio can be embedded in a RAM-style resource or use associated .sns stream data. Keep the resource set expected by the source asset; copying only the SNR header may omit the actual streamed audio.

For a header whose sample rate and sample count are understood, nominal duration is sample count divided by sample rate. File size is not a reliable substitute, and this audio duration is separate from EffectSet's normalized animation Time.

Research templates also describe a soundpipeline.bin sound registry containing name/hash and audio metadata. A historical comment claims unregistered sounds can crash the game, but that registration rule and failure mode are not verified. Treat it as an investigation point, not a confirmed engine requirement. This add-on does not create or update a sound-pipeline registry when saving EffectSet, and a file reference alone does not prove a custom sound is registered or usable.

Historical audio-inspection templates include codec-specific XAS assumptions and incomplete optional streaming/prefetch handling. They are not a general-purpose SNR encoder/decoder specification. The EffectSet UI's audio label does not imply that it can encode all listed EA codecs or convert arbitrary WAV files into game resources.

docs.title: 4. Align Sound and FX with the Clip
docs.text:
Time (0..1) is normalized progress through the full clip, not seconds, milliseconds, or a Blender frame index. For an event at elapsed time $t$ in a clip lasting $D$ seconds:

$$ \text{Time} = \frac{t}{D} $$

For a two-second clip with an event at 0.8 seconds, enter 0.4. For a five-second Spawn clip, 0.6 means three seconds, not 0.6 seconds.

AnimationSet marker Time is also normalized 0..1. If the same full clip has an Attack marker at 0.4, using 0.4 for a sound keyframe is a deliberate way to align them. There is no live synchronization: changing the marker does not move EffectSet keyframes, and changing an effect keyframe does not update animation timing metadata.

For a cast whose Cast→Resolve split is 0.35, an event intended at that split uses 0.35 on that full clip. Do not renormalize it to the shorter preview segment. Imported clips can carry their own FPS/frame-length metadata, so verify clip duration through Clip Timing... in AnimationSet rather than relying only on the current scene's FPS.

docs.title: Example: Attack Release Sound
docs.text:
1. In AnimationSet, identify the Action used by the existing Attack mapping. Preview its selected variant and note the marker fraction at the desired contact/release pose.
  2. In EffectSet, add a new entry and select that exact Action.
  3. Add a keyframe and change the default FX1 type to Audio.
  4. Set Time to the intended fraction, then enter a known working .snr/.wav reference in its first variant. Keep one variant at weight 100 while diagnosing timing.
  5. Add a separate FX keyframe if a visual resource is also required. Use an appropriate known working FX type and .fxb reference; a single keyframe has only one type.
  6. Save both editors, save the .blend, export the DRS/SKA files, and test in game. Repeat for every motion variant that needs its own event entry.

docs.title: Example: Spawn or Cast Cue
docs.text:
Use the Action from the existing Spawn or cast mapping, not an assumed ability-name match. Set the sound/FX keyframe at the desired normalized moment, checking a Spawn marker or cast split only as a visual reference. This schedules a cue; it does not determine when a unit becomes controllable, when damage resolves, or when a projectile spawns.

Sources: Time property, AnimationSet marker and timing controls.

docs.title: 5. Review Parameters Without Guessing Their Semantics
docs.text:
Field Practical guidance Min Falloff, Max Falloff Stored falloff parameters. Use values from comparable working audio/effects; the add-on provides no distance preview or documented unit calibration. Keep a sensible minimum/maximum ordering. Volume Stored floating-point value, defaulting to 1 for newly added keyframes. No Blender audition is provided. Do not assume it is a decibel value. Pitch Min, Pitch Max Stored pitch-shift range. Preserve established values; the UI does not establish whether the engine interprets them as ratios, semitones, or another scale. Offset Stored XYZ offset. The format source itself marks its spatial interpretation as uncertain; it is not a bone picker or an automatic locator binding. Verify coordinate interpretation in game. Interruptable Stored boolean flag with this exact UI spelling. Engine interruption behavior is not simulated or fully explained by the editor. Condition An incompletely understood conditional field. Do not treat it as a gameplay rule editor; preservation is currently unreliable, as described below. Variant Weight Integer 0..255 in this panel, stored as an unsigned byte. There is no sum validation or normalization despite the % list label.

For a simple two-resource example, 80 and 20 makes intent easy to read, but the panel does not prove exact engine probability semantics. Avoid all-zero sets and verify resource selection in game. Sound/FX weights here have a different UI range from AnimationSet's 0..100 motion weights.

Locators such as spell or projectile attachment points are a separate mechanism. Use the Advanced Locators Guide for the actual locator types and parenting controls. Do not assume that an EffectSet Offset or animation marker automatically attaches an FX resource to one of them.

Sources: editable properties, binary parameter definitions and uncertainties.

docs.title: What Blender Does Not Preview
docs.text:
The registered EffectSet panel has no sound audition, FX simulation, or effect-timing playback button. A Play (Anim Only) operator exists in the source but is not included in this editor's registered class list or drawn controls; do not expect it as an available panel feature.

Use AnimationSet preview or normal Blender animation playback to inspect motion and note the intended pose/time. That confirms neither resource loading nor engine spatialization, pitch, volume, conditions, permanent-effect behavior, or gameplay synchronization. AnimationSet preview may also choose the control rig, whereas SKA export uses the deform armature; see the export Action checklist.

docs.title: Export Checklist
docs.text:
1. Save the EffectSet editor and AnimationSet editor to the correct active root; save the .blend separately.
  2. Use a DRS model type that supports the intended animated model. Animated Object exports intentionally remove non-Idle AnimationSet jobs and animation markers/timings; use Animated Unit for those richer unit mappings.
  3. Ensure every required clip exists on disk. Export All SKA Actions exports saved AnimationSet references, not Actions appearing only in EffectSet or every Action in the .blend.
  4. Choose the SKA prefix strategy deliberately. The shared map rewrites DRS AnimationSet, marker-set and EffectSet animation references consistently when they resolve to the same Action. Missing/ambiguous Action resolution can still produce mismatches; inspect the exported files.
  5. Supply external sound/FX assets separately in the expected game-resource layout. This editor writes references, not the assets themselves.
  6. Reimport a copy of the output, compare its event records with the source, then test audio/FX in the game. Keep the original input and .blend until the round trip is verified.

Sources: unregistered animation-only operator and class list, EffectSet export, referenced-only SKA export, model-type filtering.

docs.title: 7. Round-Trip Limitations
docs.text:
These are current implementation boundaries, not settings that can be fixed by guessing different engine values:

  • Imported sound containers are not editable/preserved by panel Save. Import conversion captures impact_sounds and additional_sounds, but the UI state and Save serializer only reconstruct effects. Save also reseeds header defaults/checksum rather than merging all imported metadata, despite comments suggesting preservation. Back up before saving an imported EffectSet containing these records.
  • Retargeting an imported entry can retain its old SKA reference. Serialization prefers the imported hidden raw_ska over the current dropdown Action. To intentionally retarget using the UI, create a fresh entry with the intended Action and recreate its keyframes, then remove the old entry in a backup copy. Check the resulting reference after export.
  • Condition is not a reliable round-trip control. The binary class reads/writes condition, but the editor's conversion helpers use uk. Imported non-default values may be lost and edits may not reach the binary field. The binary field is signed-byte data for applicable EffectSet types, while the UI permits values up to 255; do not rely on the UI range as a format guarantee.
  • No automatic repair of resource references or timing. Invalid names, empty variants, incorrect offsets and mistimed events are not diagnosed by a successful Save. Keyframe order is preserved as edited, not sorted by time.

Sources: state-only serializer, header defaults, import conversion, export conversion, actual Condition field.

docs.title: 8. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Checks No sound/FX in Blender Expected: the panel does not audition resources or simulate FX. Verify motion separately and test the exported content in game. No event in game Confirm the game uses that exact SKA, the entry has keyframes/nonempty resources, type matches resource category, edits were saved, and assets are deployed. Sound at the wrong pose Check normalized full-clip Time, clip duration/FPS metadata, and whether the marker/split changed independently. Only one attack variant has effects Add/check entries for all required SKA clips; motion and effect variants are separate. New Action chosen but old clip still referenced Imported raw_ska takes precedence; recreate the entry rather than trusting the dropdown alone. SKA missing although EffectSet names it Add the required motion mapping in AnimationSet, or export the clip separately. EffectSet-only references do not trigger automatic SKA output. FX appears at an unexpected position Compare Offset and the existing effect's own configuration; locator attachment and marker Position are separate mechanisms. Do not guess coordinate conventions. Imported impact/extra sounds or Condition disappear Current preservation limitations; restore the backup and use a workflow that retains those records. A UI Save is not a lossless pass-through.

docs.title: Advanced Locators Guide
docs.text:
Locators describe attachment points and functional positions: a health-bar offset, a projectile origin, a bone-following effect, or a referenced module. This guide covers editing those entries, preserving their coordinate spaces, and getting scene changes into the exported CDrwLocatorList.

Two rules prevent most export mistakes: the model collection's saved locator data, not viewport geometry, is exported; and bone-attached locators must remain attached to their bones, not be reparented directly to GameOrientation.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
• Start with an imported, working asset of the same kind whenever possible. Preserve its skeleton, locator types, and resource-reference conventions until replacements have been verified in-game.
  • Make the top-level DRSModel_<basename> collection the active Layer Collection in the Outliner. Selecting a mesh, armature, or SLocators_Collection is not equivalent.
  • Open the 3D Viewport sidebar (N) → DRS Editor → CDrwLocatorList.
  • Keep the model's armature, and GameOrientation if used, inside this model's collection tree. The editor finds the first armature whose name does not contain Control_Rig; multiple candidate armatures can make attachment ambiguous.
  • Keep a saved .blend backup before changing attachment rules or deleting entries.

docs.title: Which export types contain locators?
docs.text:
The current WriteOrder includes CDrwLocatorList for AnimatedUnit. The listed static/animated object and building export types do not include this block. Creating locator markers or a blob does not add a locator block to those formats automatically. A model's appearance or its use as a building does not, by itself, establish support for unit-style locators.

For buildings, distinguish locator attachments from effects and audio, construction data, and the building's own mesh/state setup. Follow the Building Creation Guide and the requirements of a matching working asset rather than changing the export type solely to obtain locators.

docs.title: Locator Types: Choose a Role, Not a Required Set
docs.text:
These are the exact Type labels exposed by the editor. Their names describe intended roles; the add-on does not validate the game's requirements for a particular asset. Not every unit needs every type, and a type label alone does not make the associated gameplay behavior work.

ID Type Practical role / authoring guidance 0 HealthBar A position for the health-bar/UI offset. Start from the placement of a comparable working unit. 1 DestructiblePart Attachment for a referenced destructible module; the importer can load its static BMS mesh preview. 2 Construction Construction-related point; preserve the reference asset's usage rather than assuming a universal setup. 3 Turret Turret-related entry. In the current importer, a non-empty File is loaded as an SKA animation on the model's armature, not as a generic turret mesh. 4 FxbIdle Idle-effect role. Verify the referenced effect and activation behavior against the asset. 5 Wheel Wheel/module attachment; the importer attempts to load an animated BMS module and its animations. 6 StaticPerm Static permanent-effect role; retain the working asset's conventions. 7 Unknown7 Unresolved role. Preserve existing entries unless their behavior is known. 8 DynamicPerm Dynamic permanent-effect role; check attachment and resource behavior in-game. 9–13 DamageFlameSmall, DamageFlameSmallSmoke, DamageFlameLarge, DamageSmokeOnly, DamageFlameHuge Damage-effect positions. These labels are not a requirement to add all five. 14–16 SpellCast, SpellHitAll, Hit Spell/cast/hit-related positions; match the asset's actual effect and animation setup. 29 Projectile_Spawn Projectile-origin position/orientation where the game uses this role. Confirm direction and timing in-game.

docs.title: What belongs in File?
docs.text:
File becomes the locator's file_name string. It is a resource reference, not a sound-event editor or an automatic resource-packaging step.

  • Leave it empty when the locator only defines a position and the asset does not require a resource there.
  • Use the exact resource name/path expected by a working asset and the game. The editor stores the text as entered; it does not validate, copy, or convert the referenced resource. Do not assume Blender's file picker turns an absolute disk path or a // path into a usable game reference.
  • For DestructiblePart and Wheel, the current preview loaders resolve the reference relative to the imported DRS directory. A trailing .module is replaced with .bms, and the BMS supplies the referenced DRS mesh/state data.
  • For Turret, the current importer passes a non-empty reference to the SKA animation reader relative to the DRS directory. Do not substitute an arbitrary .module because the type sounds like a model attachment.
  • .fxb references can describe effects, but the locator importer does not currently build their effect visualization. A marker sphere is not evidence that the effect resource was found or will run.
  • Configure audio variants such as .snr/.wav, sound types, and animation-keyed events in the EffectSet workflow, not by placing an audio filename in a locator. See the Advanced Effects Guide.

No concrete game resource filenames are prescribed here: use references verified in the installed/extracted assets being targeted.

docs.title: 1. Create or choose an entry
docs.text:
1. Activate the correct top-level DRSModel_<basename> collection and open CDrwLocatorList.
  2. Click Add, choose Type in the dialog, and confirm; or select an existing row.
  3. Select the intended row explicitly. Selecting a row selects its matching scene object when one exists.

New entries start with an empty File, no bone attachment, zero position, and identity rotation. The editor normally creates a small mesh sphere named Locator_<Type> under SLocators_Collection; locators are not necessarily Blender Empty objects. Imported module previews can instead be meshes or armatures.

Sync existing viewport edits before Add or another detail update. These operations reapply saved data to the model's locators, so unsaved scene offsets on other entries can be overwritten too.

docs.title: 2. Set metadata and attachment before positioning
docs.text:
Under Selected Locator:

  1. Choose Type and enter File, if applicable.
  2. If the locator must follow a bone, choose it in Parent. If it is a model-root point, leave Parent empty.
  3. Click Update parent and remove transformations to commit those fields.

This button resets the selected entry's stored position to zero and rotation to identity every time, even if the parent did not change or only File was edited. A bone locator resets to its bone-local origin; a non-bone locator resets to the game-space origin, displayed through GameOrientation when available. It is not a keep-world-transform reparent command or Blender's Apply Transforms command.

The optional popup editor also shows Position (view). It is not the placement workflow: the update operator resets position rather than saving an entered offset. Position the actual scene object after the detail update.

docs.title: 3. Position the scene object, then save its transform
docs.text:
1. Select the matching locator marker or module root in the viewport/Outliner.
  2. Move and rotate it to the required point. Keep the intended parent and avoid introducing scale as a substitute for placement.
  3. For a bone attachment, scrub relevant animations and check that the point follows the correct bone.
  4. Reactivate the top-level DRSModel_<basename> collection if selecting a child changed the active Layer Collection.
  5. Click Sync from Scene. This captures scene transforms into the saved locator data and reapplies the attachment rules.
  6. Save the .blend file after synchronizing.

If metadata must change later, expect the update button to reset the offset: note the intended placement, commit the metadata, reposition the object, and sync again.

docs.title: 4. Remove through the editor
docs.text: Use Remove for an entry that should not export. It removes the saved entry and its matching scene object. Deleting only a viewport marker does not remove the saved entry; synchronization can recreate it.

docs.title: GameOrientation and Attachment Spaces
docs.text:
GameOrientation (GO) is the model's game/display-space helper, not an export prerequisite or a universal replacement for bone parenting. The standard conversion includes a Y-axis mirror and rotations about X and Z, so treating it as only an ordinary rotation can produce incorrect offsets.

Good practice, not mandatory ordering: establish the model hierarchy early to make its coordinate spaces easier to reason about. Modeling first and then parent → correct rotation → apply the relevant mesh transforms is also a supported workflow; check the resulting game-space orientation and resync locator placement afterward. Not every mesh needs a direct GO parent: imported armature hierarchies and bone-locator relationships should remain intact.

That mesh workflow is not a reason to apply transforms blindly to locator markers or imported armatures. Sync reads a locator's object transform, not the position/orientation baked into its sphere's vertices. Place/rotate the locator object and sync it; baking that placement into the marker mesh can lose the intended exported point.

Locator attachment Scene representation used by the editor What Sync from Scene records No bone; GO found Object parent is GameOrientation; saved game-space transform is displayed through GO. For a direct GO child, removes GO's world transform from the object's world transform and stores game-space position/3×3 matrix; normally bone_id = -1. Valid bone Object parent is the armature, with parent_type = BONE and the selected bone. The armature may itself sit under GO. Object-local location and matrix_basis 3×3 matrix; the parent bone's index in that armature's bone list. GO is not stripped separately from this local offset. No bone and no recognized GO parent No helper conversion is applied during capture. The object's world transform is stored directly. An arbitrary parent or indirect GO ancestor is not treated as the direct-GO case.

The editor materializes a non-bone entry by multiplying its saved game-space transform by GO's world matrix; it captures a direct GO child's transform using the inverse operation. With no GO helper, those saved values are used as world-space values instead.

Do not manually parent every locator to GO. Set attachment through Parent and the update button. Bone-following points must remain bone-attached; otherwise Sync will classify them as non-bone and lose that attachment. For a new manually created non-bone marker, establish its intended game-space placement before syncing; merely using “Keep Transform” to reparent can preserve the wrong space.

The locator editor searches for the exact object name GameOrientation inside the active model's collection tree. A helper renamed to GameOrientation.001 is not found by this lookup. This matters when multiple models are imported into one scene. Resolve helper naming/model isolation deliberately; do not compensate by rotating every locator or changing bone parents.

docs.title: The special -2 option
docs.text:
When an armature exists and Parent is empty, the editor exposes If None set Parent to -2. Committing the update writes bone_id = -2 instead of -1; the option is described as allowing attachment to a bone specified in an effect. It is still a non-bone entry in Blender, not a selection of bone index 2.

Use it only when the target asset/effect calls for it. For an imported -2 entry, confirm the checkbox and commit it before positioning and syncing: import stores the numeric ID, whereas non-bone Sync chooses -2 from the saved checkbox flag. As with other detail updates, committing the option resets the offset.

docs.title: Exactly What Sync from Scene Does
docs.text:
Sync from Scene scans recursively through the active model collection, not just the selected marker or SLocators_Collection. It recognizes objects with the _cdrw_uid custom property or names beginning with Locator_.

  • Matches existing entries by _cdrw_uid; assigns UIDs and appends entries for newly recognized objects.
  • Records bone-local transforms for actual bone parents; otherwise records the non-bone transform according to the GO rules above.
  • Updates class_id from an object's _class_id property when present. For a newly discovered marker without saved metadata, it infers the class from an exact Locator_<Type> name, otherwise defaults to HealthBar.
  • Retains an existing entry's File; it does not read a resource reference from the object's _file property. New scene-discovered entries start with an empty File.
  • Never removes saved entries merely because their scene objects were deleted.
  • Reapplies saved data to the scene and refreshes the list after capture.

Changing Type, File, Parent, or the -2 checkbox in the UI is not committed by Sync. Use Update parent and remove transformations, then place the object and sync. Use Add rather than duplicating a locator object: duplicating its UID can make two objects compete for one saved entry. Renaming an existing marker does not replace its saved type/file metadata.

docs.title: Persistence, Previews, and Export
docs.text:
The authoritative data is the CDrwLocatorListJSON custom property on the model collection. It contains the version and locator entries, including their UIDs, class IDs, resource strings, bone IDs, position, rotation matrix, and preserved unknown integer. UIDs connect this data to scene objects; they are not exported as gameplay identifiers.

  • DRS import saves the blob before optional module/locator visualization. Disabling Import Modules/Locators can leave valid locator data with no visible markers.
  • Simply opening the list reads the saved data; it does not build missing previews. Sync can materialize missing objects, but it first captures any recognized objects already present, so use a backup and inspect the result.
  • Add, the detail update, and Sync materialize generic marker spheres when no matching object exists. They do not rebuild a referenced BMS module or an FXB simulation just because File changed.
  • With Import Modules/Locators enabled, DestructiblePart/Wheel can load module previews. A non-empty Turret reference loads animation and returns without creating its own locator marker. Missing referenced files may cause import failures; preserving the blob does not supply those files.
  • Export copies the blob to its working collection and converts that saved data to SLocator entries when the selected export type includes CDrwLocatorList. It does not perform an automatic scene sync or discover markers as a fallback.
  • Missing locator data produces an empty list with a warning; malformed JSON is not a supported recovery path. Reimport a working source or restore a backup rather than hand-editing an uncertain blob.

A sphere moving correctly in Blender proves only the scene attachment. Resource availability, effect activation, projectile direction, and gameplay behavior still need a matching game asset and an in-game check.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check / correction No valid DRSModel selected. Make a direct child of the scene named DRSModel_<basename> the active Layer Collection. A nested model collection or selected object is insufficient. No armature in this model or no Parent field Ensure the intended armature is inside this model's collection tree and is not a Control_Rig. Do not pick an unrelated preview armature. Locator snaps to an origin after updating Expected: the detail update resets stored translation/rotation. Place it afterward and use Sync. Sync other pending edits before any operation that reapplies the blob. Bone-following point becomes static Check actual bone parenting, not just the UI's pending Parent value. Commit the parent, reposition, and sync; do not reparent the point directly to GO. Offset is rotated/mirrored, or differs after Sync If GO is used, check its exact name and direct non-bone parenting; otherwise confirm the intended world/game-space values. Do not apply a second conversion or strip GO from a bone-local offset. File/type edit disappears or exports unchanged Commit with Update parent and remove transformations. Sync captures scene data, not unsaved UI metadata or _file. Reposition after committing. Deleted locator returns Use Remove; scene deletion alone leaves the saved entry intact. Duplicate or unexpected HealthBar entries Inspect manually named Locator_* objects and duplicated UIDs. Prefer Add; new name inference requires an exact type label, not an arbitrary name or .001 suffix. A -2 attachment becomes -1 after Sync Commit If None set Parent to -2 before repositioning/syncing. The non-bone capture uses the saved option flag. Entry exists but has no marker, module, or effect preview Check import options and the type-specific preview behavior above. A missing preview does not imply a missing saved entry. Export ignores viewport edits or all locators Sync the correct model first; verify its blob and that the chosen export type actually includes CDrwLocatorList. There is no marker-scan export fallback. Bone attachment is wrong after skeleton changes The editor stores bone-list indices; import resolves stored skeleton identifiers. Keep the working skeleton mapping stable and revalidate attachments after bone additions/reordering.

docs.title: Before placement
docs.text:
• The intended top-level DRSModel_<basename> is active.
  • The export type supports the locator block.
  • Each chosen type serves an asset-specific purpose; no unverified “required set” was added.
  • Resource references come from verified assets; audio is configured in EffectSet instead.
  • Parent/type/file changes have been committed before positioning.

docs.title: Before export
docs.text:
• Bone locators are still attached to the intended bones; non-bone placement uses the intended GO or world/game-space convention.
  • If GO is used, its helper naming is unambiguous; the model's armature lookup is also unambiguous.
  • Placement/orientation has been checked through representative animations.
  • Sync from Scene has captured final placement on the correct model.
  • Unwanted entries were removed through Remove, with no duplicate UIDs remaining.
  • The .blend was saved after synchronization, and referenced resources are available separately.
  • Reimport/export placement and the intended in-game behavior have been checked; viewport previews alone were not treated as validation.
