docs.title: Advanced Shading Guide
docs.text:
Use this guide to prepare DRS materials, choose texture channels, and edit the material data written by the exporter. The same material workflow applies to static objects, units, and building meshes; their collection and animation setup is covered in the creation guides.

Preview is not export. The Blender shader previews selected DRS features. Export collects images, repacks parameter channels, and writes material flags, refraction color, flow vectors, and wind values. It does not bake an arbitrary Blender shader or guarantee identical in-game lighting, transparency, or animation.

docs.title: 1. Start with the DRS material layout
docs.text:
1. Use an imported DRS material as a reference, or assign the bundled DRS Material asset from the Asset Browser's DRS_Material catalog. Scene initialization registers the Battleforge Assets library; choose it or All Libraries in the browser.
  2. Select your render mesh inside Meshes_Collection. The material panels also accept meshes in GroundDecal_Collection.
  3. Open the Shading workspace and make the intended material the object's active material. The exporter reads that material, not a separate material for every face slot. Split objects when different exported materials are needed.
  4. Assign images to the existing labeled texture nodes. Keep a valid active UV map on the mesh: export calculates tangents and reads those UVs.
  5. In the 3D Viewport sidebar (N), open DRS Editor → Material. Use Flags (bool_parameter), Flow, Wind, and Cubemap Helper for object-level settings.

Flags, flow, and wind belong to the object. Shader links and images belong to the material. If two meshes need independent previews or texture assignments, make their materials single-user before changing them.

docs.title: Names are part of the integration
docs.text:
Do not rename or replace the exporter-used nodes while reorganizing the graph:

  • DRS Shader is the named Principled BSDF node, not the processing group.
  • AIO DRS Engine is the group label; its node name is DRS_Engine_Group and its node-tree name is AIO_DRS_Engine.
  • Keep the texture labels in the table below, plus Separate Metallic, Separate Roughness, Separate Emission, Separate Flu Mask, and Refraction Color.
  • Keep Apply Flu Mask and Mix Refraction Shader: UI callbacks use those labels to enable or mute preview branches.

The runtime builder's layout is the reference if an older asset has different nodes. Merely renaming an unrelated shader does not reproduce its supported connections. See the material builder.

docs.title: 2. Texture suffixes and channels
docs.text:
Suffixes identify the generated texture roles; the material's node labels and assigned images are also important for discovery. Renaming an image file alone does not enable its export.

Suffix Image node label Verified use Export condition / format _col Color Map (_col) Color feeds base color and emission color. Alpha feeds the opacity preview when alpha test or decal mode is enabled. Required image; DXT5 DDS. _nor Normal Map (_nor) Color passes through Blender's Normal Map node. The importer sets Non-Color. Use Normal Map (Bit 17); DXT1 DDS. _par Parameter Map (_par) R = metallic, G = roughness, B = flu mask, A = emission strength. The importer sets Non-Color and Channel Packed alpha. Use Parameter Map (Bit 16); repacked DXT5 DDS. _flu Flu Map Layer 1, Flu Map Layer 2 Tileable color image; import assigns the same sRGB image to both preview layers. Bit 16 and a detected flu image; one DXT5 DDS, not two independent layer textures. _ref Refraction Map (_ref) Color controls the internal refraction/transparent preview mix; alpha controls the final opaque/refraction mix. Refraction Color is a separate RGB value. Import sets the map to Non-Color. Effective Bit 18 and a detected refraction image; DXT5 DDS. _env Environment Cubemap (_env) Model-level image on the cubemap helper, not an ordinary mesh texture node. Use Env/Cube Map (Bit 18) with an assigned helper image; DXT5 cubemap.

The _par green channel is used directly as roughness in the Blender graph; it is not inverted into smoothness. The separate numeric smoothness entry in the DRS format is not this texture channel.

Engine interpretation versus add-on convention: the table documents the current Blender shader and exporter packing. Older research-template comments suggested red might be ambient occlusion, green specular, and blue roughness when no flu map is present. Those are historical hypotheses, not confirmed engine semantics. Keep the current channel layout; do not swap channels or label the old interpretation as verified without controlled in-game comparisons.

Likewise, historical Paint.NET notes recommending DXT3 for color or DXT1 for refraction are not the current export settings and do not establish an exclusive list of engine-supported DDS formats. The formats in the table describe what this add-on currently generates.

docs.title: Combined parameter map: recommended baseline
docs.text:
1. Prepare one RGBA image with the packing shown above. Preserve alpha: here it carries emission, not opacity.
  2. Assign it to Parameter Map (_par); use Non-Color and Channel Packed alpha when assigning a new image manually.
  3. Leave the group's Use Separate Maps input off, and enable Use Parameter Map (Bit 16) in the sidebar.
  4. Clear unused images from the Separate … nodes. Export prefers assigned separate metallic, roughness, and emission images over the combined image, even when Use Separate Maps is off in the preview.

A flu mask of zero selects the color-map side of the preview mix; a mask of one selects the animated flu-color side. Emission strength uses _par alpha, while the emission color comes from _col.

docs.title: Separate maps: channel-aware authoring
docs.text:
The graph exposes Separate Maps (Artist Override) and the Use Separate Maps group input. This input switches the preview between combined and separate sources; it is not a DRS flag and does not by itself select export sources.

The packing helper reads the following channels from its resolved images:

Source Channel copied into exported _par Metallic source Red → R Roughness source Green → G Flu-mask source Blue → B Emission source Alpha → A

For RGB grayscale metallic or roughness images, put the intended value in all RGB channels. A separate RGBA emission image must carry the intended strength in alpha, not only in RGB. The separate preview inputs use the image's Color output, so an emission image whose RGB and alpha differ can preview differently from its export.

The packer accepts either one shared image for all resolved channels, or a distinct image for every supplied channel. Partially reused images mixed with different images are rejected. Distinct images must have identical width and height. Unresolved channels are filled with 0, not the shader socket's preview default. The group's declared separate-input defaults are metallic 0, roughness 0.8, emission 0, and flu mask 0; linked nodes can override those preview defaults.

Current flu-mask limitation: the standard export path first resolves the group's Flu Mask output by searching upstream for an image whose label contains _par. With the generated graph, this favors the combined parameter image; an image assigned only to Separate Flu Mask is not a reliable exported B source. For fluid materials, prefer a combined _par and check its blue channel after export. Do not assume the visible separate-mask preview proves it was written.

These are image-packing rules, not shader evaluation: procedural nodes, ramps, scalar defaults, and arbitrary graph edits are not baked into parameter textures. See create_mesh and the packing helper.

docs.title: 3. Material flags: supported controls versus unknowns
docs.text:
Open Material → Flags (bool_parameter). New object properties start with Raw bool_parameter = 0; imported objects are populated from their file. Prefer the labeled toggles over manual raw-integer edits, because the toggles also update the supported preview connections.

UI control Implemented Blender / export behavior Enable Alpha Test (Bit 0) Connects _col alpha to DRS Shader alpha; exported as a flag. Decal Mode (Bit 1) Also enables that alpha connection; exported as a flag. It does not create a decal mesh or projection setup. Use Parameter Map (Bit 16) Connects _par data for preview; gates _par and _flu export. Use Normal Map (Bit 17) Connects the normal texture for preview; gates _nor export. Use Refraction Map (Bit 18) Requires a loaded Refraction Map (_ref) image; enables the refraction preview branch. Use Env/Cube Map (Bit 18) Requires a loaded helper image; controls helper visibility and requests _env export. Disable Receive Shadows (Bit 20) Named flag stored for export; no corresponding Blender shadow-preview callback is implemented here. Enable SH Lighting (Bit 21) Named flag stored for export; no corresponding Blender lighting-preview callback is implemented here. Unknown Bitflag … (Bit N) Uninterpreted flags. Preserve known-good imported values rather than choosing bits from their names.

With both alpha/decal flags off, the callback disconnects color alpha and sets preview alpha to 1. With either enabled, it uses the color image's Straight alpha mode. This is not evidence that every in-game alpha/decal rendering detail is reproduced.

The refraction and environment controls are two sources for the same exported Bit 18, not two independent file bits. Export recomputes that bit from enabled paths that actually have images; setting the raw integer alone cannot substitute for the required assets. The refraction-data writer then checks this effective bit, so an assigned _ref image can also be written when only the environment path enabled Bit 18. Clear an unused refraction image rather than relying solely on its preview toggle.

docs.title: 4. Normal maps
docs.text:
1. Assign the image to Normal Map (_nor) and use Non-Color.
  2. Enable Use Normal Map (Bit 17) on each mesh that needs it.
  3. Keep the generated connection through AIO DRS Engine → Normal → DRS Shader and keep a valid UV layout.

The exporter resolves an image rather than baking normal-processing nodes, then converts it to DXT1. No extra normal-channel inversion is performed by the shown material builder or packing path. If a source asset uses a different convention, compare against a working imported material instead of assuming a green-channel flip is required.

docs.title: Refraction map and color
docs.text:
1. Load an image into Refraction Map (_ref) before enabling Use Refraction Map (Bit 18). An enable attempt without an image is rejected with a notice.
  2. Set the Refraction Color RGB node; the generated node defaults to white (1, 1, 1).
  3. Inspect the material in a shading mode that evaluates its nodes. The preview uses a glass/transparent branch, the parameter-map roughness, and the normal-map result. Enabling the branch also enables backface culling; disabling it mutes the branch and disables that culling setting.
  4. Check the exported texture and RGB value after a round trip. Changing internal glass IOR, mix nodes, or other Blender-only settings does not serialize those shader edits into DRS.

The preview wiring establishes how Blender uses the map, not a complete specification of the game's refraction algorithm. When Bit 18 is inactive, export writes a zero refraction color. When active, it reads the labeled Refraction Color node; if that node cannot be found, the export fallback is black.

docs.title: Model-level environment helper
docs.text:
1. Select a mesh under the intended DRSModel_<basename> root and open Material → Cubemap Helper.
  2. Click Add Cubemap (Earth Base). This creates or resets Environment_Collection / Environment_Cubemap using the bundled earth cubemap when available. Check Model Cubemap → Assigned, not just that a helper object exists.
  3. To use a custom image, select the helper and replace the image on Environment Cubemap (_env) in its material. Keep that node label/name and the helper collection intact. Re-select the render mesh afterward.
  4. Enable Use Env/Cube Map (Bit 18) for each mesh that should request the model's cubemap. Adding the helper alone is not that per-mesh export request.
  5. Use Debug Export Cubemap to check conversion independently. It writes a timestamped DDS to the add-on's sr_impex/debug folder; it is not a complete model export. Remove Cubemap removes the model helper, so check all dependent meshes afterward.

The export converter supports square-face 6×1 horizontal strips, 1×6 vertical strips, and a 4×3 cross. Strip order is +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z (left-to-right or top-to-bottom). The cross uses this layout; each entry is one square tile:

Column 1 Column 2 Column 3 Column 4 Top — +Y — — Middle -X +Z +X -Z Bottom — -Y — —

The helper's automatic preview UV layout supports strips only; a cross can be accepted by export without receiving a correct helper preview. The helper is a textured emission cube, not a Blender world-lighting or reflection-capture system. Do not judge in-game environment behavior from its visibility alone. Cubemap conversion requires the bundled texconv.exe and texassemble.exe.

docs.title: 6. Flu animation and Flow
docs.text:
1. Set up _par with a nonzero blue mask where flu color should appear and enable Bit 16.
  2. Assign the same tileable image to Flu Map Layer 1 and Flu Map Layer 2. The generated preview repeats the images and crossfades two animated coordinate layers; export selects one flu image, so different images in the two nodes are not a supported two-texture export setup.
  3. Open Material → Flow and enable Write Flow when the four flow vectors should be written to the mesh material block.
  4. Set the vectors using a working imported asset as a starting point. Play or scrub the timeline to inspect the preview, then reimport an export to check the stored values.
Flow control New-object default What is verified Write Flow Off Enables vector export; it is separate from the texture-enable flag. Max Flow Speed (0, 0, 0, 0) Four stored components; XYZ feeds preview MaxSpeed. Min Flow Speed (0, 0, 0, 0) XYZ feeds preview MinSpeed. Flow Speed Change (0, 0, 0, 0) XYZ feeds preview Frequency. Flow Scale (0, 0, 0, 0) XYZ feeds preview Scale, multiplying generated coordinates.

The UI declares no extra min/max bounds for these vectors. All four components are exported when Write Flow is enabled, but the fourth component is not used by this preview. Its in-game meaning and the engine's units are not established here. The preview group interface starts with scale (1, 1, 1), whereas object Flow properties start at zero; those are different defaults. A zero scale collapses the preview's spatial coordinate variation.

Write Flow gates serialization, not the shader's time driver. Conversely, Bit 16 gates _par/_flu texture export but does not automatically enable Write Flow. The preview's frame-driven oscillation is an approximation, not a measured copy of game timing.

docs.title: 7. Wind
docs.text:
Open Material → Wind. If the mesh has no generated wind modifier, click Add Wind Modifier; the controls remain disabled until a WindEffect Geometry Nodes modifier exists. Imported render meshes normally receive this modifier during material creation.

Control New-object default Declared UI range / preview use Wind Response 0.0 0.0–0.1; multiplies scene time before the preview's noise node. Wind Height 0.0 No explicit min/max bounds; lower threshold for the preview's height falloff.

The current preview measures local Y, uses the mesh's local Y bounding-box span for the falloff's upper endpoint, and offsets positions along local X. It is not a world-Z height slider. Recheck the preview after editing mesh orientation or dimensions. Keep the modifier's Wind Response and Wind Height node names if editing its graph.

Export stores these two object values in the material entries for wind response and wind height. It does not serialize the Geometry Nodes graph as an engine wind simulation. More generally, the exporter creates the numeric Materials block from defaults and overrides these wind entries; arbitrary Principled settings are not converted into the format's other numeric material parameters.

docs.title: 8. Export and verification checklist
docs.text:
• Each render mesh has the intended active material, a valid active UV map, and the expected DRS node layout.
  • Color Map (_col) has a loaded image. Missing color data aborts mesh export; a flat Blender base color is not a replacement.
  • Bit 16/17 and refraction/environment toggles match the images actually assigned. Clear stale separate-map images before using a combined _par.
  • Parameter sources use a supported packing pattern and matching dimensions; emission is in alpha, and the exported blue flu mask is checked explicitly.
  • Both flu preview layers use the same image. Write Flow is enabled only when its vectors should be written.
  • Cubemap conversion succeeds, and required conversion executables remain in the add-on's resources folder.
  • Export into a separate output folder, inspect the generated DDS files and warnings, then reimport the DRS into a separate scene to compare textures, flags, refraction RGB, flow vectors, and wind values.

The material exporter traverses supported image chains with a bounded search and role-label matching; it does not evaluate arbitrary node graphs. Prefer the generated layout to deep chains or renamed nodes. A file being created is not sufficient proof that every optional texture was exported: several missing-map and packing failures are reported without immediately aborting the whole model export.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Checks Material panels only show a selection notice Select a mesh in Meshes_Collection or GroundDecal_Collection, not an armature, helper, or the root collection. Mesh export stops at color-map setup Check the active material, DRS Shader name, Color Map (_col) image and label, and its connection to base color. _par is absent or differs from preview Enable Bit 16; inspect separate-node overrides, source channels, dimensions, and mixed reused/distinct-image errors. Preview scalar defaults are not exported texture data. Fluid color or mask disappears Check Bit 16, both flu images, packed _par blue, and the separate-flu-mask limitation above. Toggle Bit 16 off/on after assigning images to refresh the mask preview callback. Normal map is absent Enable Bit 17; check Normal Map (_nor), Non-Color, and the generated normal chain. Refraction/environment toggle turns itself off Assign the required image first. Check the sidebar notice and the helper's Assigned status. Raw Bit 18 alone is insufficient. Cubemap conversion fails Check layout dimensions, face order, the two bundled conversion tools, and the debug-export error log in sr_impex/debug. Cross preview UVs are not generated automatically. Flow seems static or uniform Check nonzero scale and speed values, timeline playback, and the flu mask. Write Flow controls export, not playback. Wind controls are disabled or falloff seems wrong Add the modifier, preserve its expected node names, and inspect local Y extent and Wind Height, not only world-space height. Two objects' previews change together Their material or processing node tree may be shared; inspect datablock users before making independent edits.

docs.text:

  • Material/Flow/Wind editor: UI labels, property defaults/ranges, flag callbacks, and preview updates.

docs.title: Related Guides
docs.text:
• Start with the Object Creation Guide.
  • For unit-specific export and animation setup, see the Unit Creation Guide.
  • For building and state-based mesh setup, see the Building Creation Guide.

docs.title: Building Creation Guide
docs.text:
Buildings add a mesh grid, mesh states, and referenced resources to the ordinary DRS mesh/material workflow. A .bmg is not simply a static .drs with a different filename.

Start with the Object Creation Guide for mesh, material, collision, and GO basics. Use the Unit Creation Guide for skeletons and SKA actions when the building is animated.

Current support boundary: Building import, state visibility, and mesh-grid editing are available. Full building export is still incomplete: the current BMG writer does not assemble the complete state/resource graph, and several animation, effect, and collision export branches remain unimplemented. The export menu and a successful completion message do not guarantee a game-ready building. Work on copies and retain the original BMG and its referenced assets.

docs.title: 1. Start from an Existing Building
docs.text:
For building work, importing a comparable building is more useful than starting with an empty object scene. It supplies the mesh-state relationships, resource names, and grid metadata that the simple scene generator does not create.

  1. Keep the source .bmg, its referenced state .drs files, textures, debris XML, and any .ska files together in their expected resource layout.
  2. Choose File > Import > Battleforge (.drs/.bmg) and select the building.
  3. Review the import options before confirming. Clear Scene is on by default; disable it if you need to keep the current scene.
  4. Save the imported setup to a new .blend file before editing it.

Useful options:

Option Purpose Apply Transform Controls the import's GO display-axis conversion. Use the same setting when comparing two imports. Import Collision Shape Imports building-level collision and eligible state collision data. Import S0 Collision Shapes Also imports collision from undamaged state DRS files; off by default because building-level collision can already represent those states. Import Debris Imports the referenced debris setup where available. Import Construction Imports referenced construction pieces. Import Animation Enables animation import for a rigged building.

A missing referenced file is a resource problem, not something that can be fixed by changing a collection's name.

docs.title: 2. Understand the Imported Structure
docs.text:
A typical imported building contains the following collection structure. Optional resources and Blender numeric suffixes vary by asset:

Text Only
DRSModel_<building>
├── GameOrientation                  (Empty object)
├── GroundDecal_Collection            (optional)
├── CollisionShapes_Collection        (building-level collision, if present)
│   ├── Boxes_Collection
│   ├── Spheres_Collection
│   └── Cylinders_Collection
├── Armature_Collection              (if the building is rigged)
├── SLocators_Collection              (construction helpers, if imported)
└── MeshSetGrid_0
    ├── MeshSet_0
    │   ├── Active_State_MeshSet_0    (Empty marker)
    │   └── States_Collection_0
    │       ├── S0_Undamaged
    │       │   └── Meshes_Collection
    │       ├── S2_Damaged
    │       │   ├── Meshes_Collection
    │       │   └── CollisionShapes_Collection (when imported)
    │       └── Debris_Collection
    │           ├── S2_Debris
    │           └── S3_Debris
    └── MeshSet_1 ...

A state can contain its own collision subcollections. The grid references individual mesh sets, and each mesh set groups its related states. Do not flatten all state meshes into the root or combine every state into one ordinary object export collection.

docs.title: GO and parenting
docs.text:
Good practice: Use the building's GO coordinate convention consistently for new meshes, collision shapes, and non-bone helpers. Parenting a new primitive before fitting it is convenient, but not a required modeling order; correcting and applying a mesh rotation after parenting is also a supported workflow.

Collection nesting is not object parenting. Inspect the actual parent relationship when adding a mesh to an imported state. Keep existing armature and bone-attached relationships intact rather than parenting every object directly to GO. Do not reset or apply GO itself to compensate for one misaligned state.

The mesh-grid visualization expects the model's GO helper to exist. Keeping that helper for the editor is different from requiring every mesh to be parented before modeling.

docs.title: 3. Inspect States in the BMG Editor
docs.text:
Open the 3D Viewport sidebar (N) and select BMG Editor > BMG Mesh State Editor.

Button What to inspect Show undamaged The S0_Undamaged meshes. Show damaged The S2_Damaged meshes on their own. Show damaged + Debris (should look undamaged) Damaged geometry together with S2_Debris; useful for checking how pieces fit. Show Debris The imported debris collections. Show All Stages All state collections together for comparison. Overlapping geometry is expected in this view.

These controls switch visibility; they do not create missing states, author debris physics, or define gameplay transitions. The Switch All States controls operate on mesh sets across the scene, so take care when several buildings are loaded.

Use Show Collision Shapes and Show SLocators to reduce clutter. Hiding a helper for editing is not a substitute for removing unwanted resource references from an export setup.

docs.title: 4. Inspect or Fit a Mesh Grid
docs.text:
Make the intended DRSModel_... root active before using the grid controls.

  • Show Mesh Grid toggles the visualization.
  • Create Grid fits new grid metadata to eligible undamaged-state meshes. It uses a fixed cell size of 2.0 and currently creates a square grid with an odd number of cells along each axis.
  • Rotation changes the editor's grid/model orientation in degrees. It is not a reason to rotate GO manually.
  • Center Pivot At Origin (0,0,0) chooses whether the grid is centered at the origin or the detected model center.
  • Remove Grid removes stored grid data and its visualization, not the building's visible meshes.

Save before recreating a grid. Create Grid rebuilds metadata and resets the grid/model rotation to zero before fitting; it is not a harmless visibility toggle. Review the result instead of assuming an imported layout or cell assignment was preserved.

The fitting code looks for meshes inside the undamaged-state Meshes_Collection hierarchy. An ordinary object scene with no S0_Undamaged meshes is not automatically a fully configured building just because the grid button is available. Empty or unexpectedly small grids are a reason to check the hierarchy and dimensions first.

A visible grid is an authoring aid, not proof that the complete BMG state graph can currently be exported.

docs.title: 5. Edit Materials, Collision, and Optional Resources
Visible meshes and materials
docs.text: Edit each state's render meshes in its own Meshes_Collection. Apply the same UV, triangulation, material, and vertex-budget checks described in the Object Creation Guide. Use the Advanced Shading Guide for packed parameters, wind, refraction, and environment maps.

docs.title: Collision
docs.text:
Keep building-level collision separate from damage-state collision. A damaged state may need a different approximation than the undamaged building.

When adding a shape, use its state's matching box/sphere/cylinder collection. As for visible meshes, using the correct model's GO is good practice; fitting the shape first and correcting its rotation after parenting is also possible. Preserve the primitive's geometry: boxes remain rectangular, spheres remain round, and cylinders remain circular and capped. See Object Creation Guide, step 8.

docs.title: Ground decal
docs.text: GroundDecal_Collection is imported when the BMG references a ground decal DRS. It is optional and distinct from both building collision and the grid visualization. A new mesh placed in this collection is not automatically wired into a complete exported building resource graph.

docs.title: Construction pieces and debris
docs.text: Preserve their referenced assets and the imported relationships. A construction helper or debris mesh is not equivalent to a finished building state. The current UI can inspect these resources, but it does not replace an external debris/resource authoring workflow.

docs.title: 6. Animated Buildings and Visual Hooks
docs.text:
Use the building's deform skeleton, skin weights, and SKA actions as described in the Unit Creation Guide. A building is not limited to one idle animation: relevant assets may use spawn, attack, casting, channeling, or turret-related animation modes.

Choose only the modes required by the target asset. A long list of available animation types is not a checklist that every building needs to implement. See the Advanced Abilities Guide for action/marker relationships and the Advanced Effects Guide for sound metadata.

Non-bone locators use the model's coordinate convention, while bone locators follow the armature. Use the Advanced Locators Guide rather than manually forcing all helpers under GO.

docs.title: 7. Save, Export Cautiously, and Validate
docs.text:
The menu File > Export > Battleforge Building (.bmg) offers static and animated building model types, mesh options, and SKA naming controls. Those UI options do not mean every corresponding BMG export branch is complete.

For now:

  1. Save the edited .blend file as the authoritative working copy.
  2. Keep the source BMG and every referenced resource unchanged in a separate location.
  3. If testing BMG export, use a disposable folder and inspect the actual files produced. The current save path can produce a .drs-suffixed file despite the BMG menu; renaming it alone does not implement the missing building data.
  4. If exporting a component DRS separately, prepare a proper standalone DRSModel_... hierarchy and follow the object/unit export guide. A nested state collection is not automatically a standalone export root.
  5. Re-import tests into a separate scene, compare matching states with the same display-axis settings, and verify resources and behavior in game before distributing anything.

docs.title: Building checklist
docs.text:
• The original BMG and referenced DRS/XML/DDS/SKA files are backed up.
  • Each mesh remains in the correct mesh set and state.
  • New geometry follows the intended GO convention without breaking existing rig/bone parents.
  • Undamaged, damaged, and debris views were checked separately.
  • Building-level and state-level collision were not accidentally confused or duplicated.
  • Grid rotation, pivot, and cell layout were checked after any rebuild.
  • Export limitations are understood; no completion message was treated as proof of a full building round trip.

docs.title: Object Creation Guide
docs.text: This guide walks through creating a new object from scratch for the SR-ImpEx Blender plugin.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
1. Install and enable the add-on in Blender, then save a working .blend file.
  2. Decide whether to modify an imported model or start from scratch. This guide covers a new static object; importing a similar existing asset is useful when you need a reference for size, materials, or collision.
  3. For a rigged object or unit, continue with the Unit Creation Guide. For building states and mesh grids, use the Building Creation Guide.
  4. Keep original game assets separate from your export folder. Test exports should never overwrite your only source copy.

Two different hierarchies: Collections determine what the exporter includes. Object parents determine coordinate space. Moving a mesh into a collection does not parent it to GameOrientation (GO). Using the model's GO is recommended for consistent viewport authoring, but parenting before modeling is a convenience, not a required order of operations.

docs.title: 1. Create a New BattleForge Scene
docs.text:
Go to File > Import > New Battleforge Scene.

A file browser window will open. You can ignore that part for now and instead use the options in the right-hand sidebar.

Select the object type you want to generate. For this tutorial, choose Static Object.

Enable Collision Support if you plan to export a collision-enabled object type. This creates the collision collections, not fitted collision meshes; those are added in step 8.

For this tutorial, enable it so the full workflow is covered. Use a comparable game asset to decide whether collision is appropriate for your object. Adding collision volumes is not, by itself, a complete definition of game-side interaction or pathing behavior.

docs.title: 2. Understand the Collection Hierarchy
docs.text:
This creates a full collection hierarchy in the Blender Outliner.

The most important collections are:

Collection What belongs here DRSModel_object_CHANGENAME Model root. Replace CHANGENAME with your model name, keeping the DRSModel_ prefix. Meshes_Collection Visible model meshes, directly in this collection. CollisionShapes_Collection Container for the three collision subcollections. Boxes_Collection Rectangular box collision meshes. Spheres_Collection Sphere collision meshes. Cylinders_Collection Circular cylinder collision meshes.

GameOrientation is an Empty object in the model root, not another collection. The exporter uses the collection hierarchy to find meshes and collision shapes; do not replace the named collections with arbitrary folders.

Tip: You can delete the default Blender collection with the camera and light, or leave it outside the model root. Keep helper objects and unrelated test meshes out of the export collections.

docs.title: 3. Understand GameOrientation (Recommended Practice)
docs.text:
The game and Blender use different coordinate conventions. GameOrientation (GO) is the model's coordinate-conversion helper; its transform includes a rotation and a mirror. It is not a second mesh or an ordinary placement control.

Good practice, not a mandatory modeling order: For a fresh primitive, parenting to the model's GO before fitting it makes the viewport workflow easier. You can also model first, parent later, correct the visible rotation, and apply the mesh rotation. The important check is the exported result, not when you created the parent relationship.

For the recommended workflow:

  1. Add a mesh and place it directly in Meshes_Collection.
  2. In Object Properties > Relations > Parent, choose this model's GameOrientation Empty. With multiple models loaded, check the model root rather than choosing another model's similarly named helper.
  3. Shape and position the geometry in Edit Mode. Object Mode rotation/scale can also be baked into a standalone mesh with Ctrl+A > Rotation & Scale when needed.

If you parent an already modeled object, its viewport orientation can change. Correct the mesh, not GO. Blender's Keep Transform parenting also creates a parent-inverse transform, so it is not identical to simply selecting a parent in Relations. Applying object rotation does not remove a parent inverse.

For ordinary render meshes, baked rotation is part of the exported vertex data; do not assume every unapplied Object Mode transform or arbitrary parent chain is exported just because it looks correct in Blender. See the round-trip check in step 10.

Leave an imported model's existing hierarchy intact unless you intentionally need to change it. In particular, do not reset GO or apply its transform to every child to make its transform fields look tidy. Rigged meshes and bone-attached locators follow their existing armature relationships; see the Unit Creation Guide and Advanced Locators Guide.

docs.title: 4. Model the Object
docs.text:
Create and sculpt your object as needed. The artistic modeling process is outside this guide, but these export requirements matter:

  • Use real mesh data. Convert non-mesh objects and bake geometry-changing modifiers on a working copy when their result needs to be exported. Do not assume the viewport's evaluated modifier result is the stored mesh.
  • Create a UV map. The exporter reads the active UV layer and calculates tangents. A textured material alone is not a substitute for UVs.
  • Keep the render geometry triangulated. Auto-fix Quad Faces can triangulate the export copy; clean up problematic faces before export rather than relying on a visual preview alone.
  • Watch vertex counts. Validation rejects a mesh with more than 32,767 vertices, and also checks the combined, welded render mesh against that limit. UV splitting can duplicate vertices, so leave headroom.
  • Use the intended material on each exported mesh. Do not assume several material slots on one object become separate game materials; use separate mesh objects for independently configured materials.
  • Check scale and forward direction against an existing asset. A correctly shaded Blender viewport does not establish the model's in-game scale or orientation.

docs.title: 5. Assign the DRS Material
docs.text:
Once you are happy with the shape, the next step is setting up the material.

Change an editor area's type to Asset Browser. Choose the Battleforge Assets library (registered by scene initialization), or All Libraries, then open the DRS_Material catalog and drag DRS Material onto the mesh.

Make it the mesh's active material. Use one intended exported material per mesh, and preserve the generated node names/labels: the exporter reads supported parts of this layout rather than baking any arbitrary Blender shader. A loaded Color Map (_col) image and a valid active UV map are part of the basic export setup.

If the asset library is missing, check Edit > Preferences > File Paths > Asset Libraries for the bundled library, or start from an imported DRS material. See the Advanced Shading Guide for the supported node layout and material-sharing caveats.

docs.title: 6. Set Up Textures
docs.text:
Open the Shading workspace, select your model, and use the shader editor to assign the textures.

Start with the supported texture roles:

Role Usual suffix Important distinction Color _col Required color image; alpha is used by supported transparency modes. Normal _nor Use a data/non-color image and enable its material flag. Packed parameters _par R metallic, G roughness, B flu mask, A emission strength. Alpha here is not color-map opacity. Flu color _flu Used with the _par mask and optional Flow metadata. Refraction _ref Has its own preview/flag setup and RGB refraction value. Environment _env Model-level cubemap helper, not an ordinary per-mesh color slot.

A matching filename suffix alone does not enable a map: assign it to the supported node and check the corresponding material controls. For packing rules, separate-map overrides, color spaces, flu animation, and environment/refraction caveats, use the Advanced Shading Guide.

docs.title: 7. Open the DRS Editor Panel
docs.text:
Select the render mesh to edit its material properties, open the 3D Viewport sidebar (N), and choose DRS Editor > Material. The material panels are object-level controls; selecting only a root collection or collision helper is not the same context.

For this tutorial, the most important sections are:

  • Flags (bool_parameter)
  • Wind

Other metadata editors and export selection use the active DRSModel_... root collection. If several models are loaded, check both the active mesh and model root before editing.

docs.title: Material Flags
docs.text:
This section lets you enable important material features such as:

  • Alpha test
  • Parameter map usage for metallic, roughness, and emission
  • Normal map usage

If you use any of those texture maps, make sure the corresponding flags are enabled.

docs.title: Wind
docs.text:
These object properties are exported as wind material values; the Geometry Nodes modifier supplies a Blender preview.

  • Wind Height: Lower threshold for the preview's height falloff; defaults to 0.
  • Wind Response: Defaults to 0, with a UI range of 0 to 0.1.

If the mesh has no generated wind modifier, click Add Wind Modifier first. Play the timeline to preview it. The current preview uses the mesh's local Y for its height calculation, not world Z, so review it after changing mesh orientation or dimensions.

The preview does not guarantee identical game wind behavior, and its modifier is not exported as an engine node graph. See Advanced Shading Guide > Wind.

docs.title: 8. Create Collision Shapes
docs.text:
If your object needs collision, this is the final setup step before export.

Use simple meshes in the matching subcollection; the collection, not the object's name, selects the exported primitive type:

Primitive Collection Keep this geometry Cube/box Boxes_Collection A rectangular box with perpendicular axes and planar faces. Sphere Spheres_Collection A round sphere. An ellipsoid cannot be represented exactly by a single sphere. Cylinder Cylinders_Collection A circular cylinder with two parallel planar caps. Caps may be n-gons or triangles.

GO reminder: As with visible meshes in step 3, using the same model's GO is good practice when fitting new collision shapes. Collection membership alone does not establish that relationship. Parenting before modeling is optional: you can create and fit a shape first, parent it later, correct its viewport rotation, and apply that rotation to the collision mesh. Do not rotate GO to correct only one shape.

A practical workflow is:

  1. Add the primitive and move it into its matching collision collection.
  2. If using GO, choose this model's helper under Object Properties > Relations > Parent.
  3. Position and size the shape against the visible model. If parenting changed its appearance, correct the mesh's rotation; Ctrl+A > Rotation can bake that correction.
  4. Set Object Properties > Viewport Display > Display As > Wire to make fitting easier.
  5. Repeat with additional shapes only where they improve the approximation.

One to five shapes is often a useful starting point, not a format limit. These are collision volumes, not extra render meshes: keep them out of Meshes_Collection and avoid bevels, sculpted surfaces, or sheared shapes that no longer describe the selected primitive. A sphere has only one radius, and a cylinder has one radius plus a height; non-uniform scaling must not turn them into ellipsoids or elliptical cylinders if you expect an exact fit.

Export and re-import a test after fitting. Check the collision shape's position, tilt, height, and radius, not just whether it is present. See the collision format notes for representation limits.

docs.title: 9. Export the Object
docs.text:
Make the root DRSModel_... collection active in the Outliner, not just a mesh, collision subcollection, or Meshes_Collection. Then choose File > Export > Battleforge Object/Unit (.drs). Menu text also includes the add-on version.

Before exporting, save the .blend file and place the 3D cursor at world origin (Shift+S > Cursor to World Origin); the export preparation uses the cursor when setting mesh origins. Choose a separate test folder.

Setting For this static-object example Model Type Choose Static Object (with collision) when you populated the collision collections, otherwise Static Object (no collision). Collision-enabled export requires collision data. Split Mesh by UV Islands Enabled by default. Keep it on unless you have a specific reason to manage UV splits yourself. Flip Normals Off by default. Use it for a confirmed winding/normal problem, not as a fix for a misplaced or rotated object. Auto-fix Quad Faces Enabled by default; triangulates the export copy. Mip Maps Auto is the default. Numeric choices cap the mip count per image; see the Advanced Shading Guide. Export All SKA Actions Not needed for this static object; disable it. Model Name Prefix Affects SKA names, not static mesh orientation. Not needed here. [DEBUG] Export SKA Tangents Not relevant to a static object. Keep Debug Collection Leave off for normal export; keeps the export copy for diagnosis when enabled.

The importer's Apply Transform option and Blender's Ctrl+A are different operations. There is no general DRS export checkbox that promises to bake every object's parent hierarchy.

docs.title: 10. Final Export Result and Round-Trip Check
docs.text: After exporting, you should find the final .drs file together with the generated .dds textures for the maps you used. Read the add-on's message log if export fails; a Blender preview alone does not establish a successful file export.

docs.title: Before considering the object finished
docs.text:
• The root retains its DRSModel_ prefix, and render meshes/collision meshes are in their correct collections.
  • Render meshes have an active UV map and a supported DRS material.
  • The selected model type matches the presence or absence of collision shapes.
  • The exported file and referenced textures exist in the test folder.
  • A fresh import matches the source model's scale and orientation, and all collision shapes fit correctly.

To check a round trip:

  1. Open a separate Blender file, or explicitly disable Clear Scene when importing into the current scene; that import option is enabled by default.
  2. Import the exported .drs with Import Collision Shape enabled.
  3. Use the same Apply Transform import setting for both sides of a comparison. Different display-axis settings can make identical data look rotated.
  4. Compare mesh silhouette, textures, collision position, and primitive dimensions. Avoid rotating only a GO helper just to line up two test copies.
  5. If the first round trip matches, export/import the test again to check that rotations or offsets do not accumulate.
  6. Validate the result in game as well. Blender previews do not reproduce every shader or gameplay behavior.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: Symptom Check first Export says the selected collection is invalid Make the DRSModel_... root active, not a child collection. A mesh does not export Put the mesh directly in Meshes_Collection; check its UVs, material, and vertex count. A mesh looks right in Blender but exports rotated Check baked mesh data, unapplied object transforms, parent inverses, and the import display-axis setting; do not change GO blindly. Collision is missing or has the wrong type Check Model Type and the box/sphere/cylinder subcollection, not just object names or viewport visibility. A cylinder changes size or tilt Keep it circular and capped, and compare a fresh round trip before adding more shape edits. Surface looks inside-out Inspect face orientation and normals; use Flip Normals only after confirming the issue. Textures or packed channels look wrong Check the Advanced Shading Guide.

docs.title: Unit Creation Guide
docs.text:
This guide walks through the basic setup for creating a unit or animated object with the SR-ImpEx Blender plugin.

First follow the shared scene, mesh, UV, and material setup in the Object Creation Guide. Do not copy the static-object collision or export choices unchanged: units and animated objects use different export types.

Target DRS export type Important difference A unit with animation/locator metadata Animated Unit Writes unit animation, effect, and locator blocks; does not export the object collision-shape block. A rigged prop or animated object Animated Object (no collision) or Animated Object (with collision) Can use simple object collision when that type is chosen. It does not gain unit locators simply by being animated. A building with states/grid resources Building export types Follow the Building Creation Guide, including its current export limitations.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
A unit or animated object needs:

  • a deform armature and its skeleton/rest pose;
  • render meshes with an Armature modifier referencing that deform armature;
  • vertex groups that match the intended deform bones, with valid skin weights;
  • Blender actions and animation metadata appropriate to the target asset.

Each vertex can use up to 4 bone influences. Clean up and normalize weights intentionally; limiting the influence count during export is not a substitute for checking the deformation.

The new-scene operator creates the shared object collections, not a finished character rig. Put the deform armature in a direct child collection named Armature_Collection and render meshes directly in Meshes_Collection. Start from an imported, compatible skeleton when possible; changing a skeleton/rest pose without checking the skin and animations can break their agreement.

docs.title: GO and rig relationships
docs.text:
Recommended practice: Keep the armature and meshes in one consistent model coordinate convention. When using GameOrientation (GO), leave the armature under the model's helper and keep skinned meshes attached to their deform armature. Parenting before modeling is convenient, not a required order of operations.

Do not reparent every skinned mesh directly to GO just because a static mesh can be authored that way. Bone-attached locators also stay attached to bones. Avoid applying transforms to GO, the armature, or an existing bound rig as a blanket rotation fix; changes to a rig need animation and skin validation, not just a still-frame check. See Object Creation Guide, step 3 for the distinction between collections, parenting, and baked mesh rotation.

docs.title: 1. Set Up the Required Locators
docs.text:
A unit also uses locators.

The following are common starting points, not a universally enforced minimum set. Match the needs of a comparable working unit and its gameplay resources. Add them through DRS Editor > CDrwLocatorList with the top-level DRSModel_... collection active:

  • HealthBar: a health-bar/UI position, commonly left without a bone parent.
  • Hit: a hit-related point; bone attachment depends on the asset.
  • Projectile_Spawn: a projectile-origin position/orientation where the asset uses that role.

Adding a locator alone does not define a projectile, damage rule, or gameplay ability. The current DRS writer includes CDrwLocatorList for Animated Unit, not the animated-object export types.

Use this order to avoid losing locator placement:

  1. Add an entry or choose an existing one, then set Type, File if needed, and Parent. A bone parent makes it follow that bone; an empty parent field is a model-root point.
  2. Click Update parent and remove transformations to commit the metadata/attachment. This resets position and rotation, so do it before final placement, not after.
  3. Move and rotate the scene locator to its intended point. Scrub an animation if it is bone-attached.
  4. Make the model root active again and click Sync from Scene. This writes scene transforms/attachments into the model's saved locator data; it is not just a UI refresh.
  5. Save the .blend file. Export reads the saved locator data, not an unsynchronized scene marker.

GO note: A non-bone locator can use the model's GO convention; a bone locator must remain bone-local. The editor manages this distinction. Do not manually reparent every locator to GO or use the parent-reset button as a keep-transform operation.

See the Advanced Locators Guide for supported types, resource references, multiple-model selection, and the difference between changing metadata and syncing scene transforms.

docs.title: 2. Understand Units vs. Animated Objects
docs.text:
A unit usually has multiple animation modes. The current animated-object export path keeps the Idle visibility job and removes unit-style markers/timings; selecting Animated Object is not a way to export a unit with fewer requirements.

The editor's initialization template provides a useful starting list, not an exporter-enforced guarantee that every unit needs exactly these animations:

  • Idle
  • Walk
  • Run
  • Spawn
  • HitFromBack
  • Cheer/Emote
  • HitFromFront
  • Die
  • HitFromLeft
  • HitFromRight
  • PushBackStandUp (Loop)

Loop animations have three parts: start, loop, and end. The loop section should be the repeated part. A good example is a unit being pushed back continuously by wind and staying inside the same repeated motion.

There are more animation types available. Check the AnimationSet Editor and a comparable working asset for the relevant set. Entries marked Not yet Supported, such as ModeSwitch, are not an authoring promise.

docs.title: Actions and saved metadata are separate
docs.text:
1. Create or import the Blender actions on the deform rig, then choose their references in the AnimationSet rows.
  2. Use Init only when you intentionally want to clear and repopulate the current editor setup; do not use it as a harmless refresh on imported metadata.
  3. Choose animation modes, variants, weights, and any markers, then click Save in the AnimationSet editor to persist them to the model collection.
  4. Save the .blend file as well. Reset reloads saved metadata; it does not save pending edits.

An action existing in Blender's Action list does not mean it is referenced by the saved AnimationSet or will be included in Export All SKA Actions.

docs.title: 3. Add Animation Variants
docs.text:
You can create multiple variants for the same animation and assign a weight to each one.

For example, if you want two idle animations and one should play most of the time, you can assign weights like this:

  • default idle: 80
  • special idle: 20

Using a total of 100 makes the intended weighting easy to review. The editor accepts individual values from 0 to 100, but does not automatically normalize or validate the total.

Other important settings:

  • Allows IK: enabled for new variants by default; metadata, not an IK-baking command.
  • Force No Blend: disabled for new variants by default; preserve deliberate imported settings.

For a unit that uses melee attacks, configure the appropriate attack mode and marker relationship required by that asset. The add-on stores the animation/visual metadata; it does not create the gameplay ability itself.

docs.title: 4. Add Markers for Important Animations
docs.text:
Some animations, especially Spawn and Attack, need a marker.

Markers store an event position and normalized point in an animation. Assets can use them for spawn, attack, and other visual/gameplay timing, but the add-on does not validate when an external gameplay system makes a unit controllable or applies a hit.

Marker Time is a fraction from 0 to 1, not seconds or a frame number. In a 5-second clip, 0.6 means 3 seconds. To target 0.6 seconds in that clip, enter 0.12.

Match the marker's animation type/visibility job to the intended mode and preview the relevant variant. Do not assume an identically named Blender action automatically creates that relationship. The editor derives timing metadata from the referenced clip and marker settings; the displayed millisecond timing fields are read-only.

Useful marker tools:

  • Display Marker: previews the animation at the selected marker time
  • Play Marker: plays the animation until the marker time so you can fine-tune the timing
  • XYZ: sets the exact 3D marker position

Place the marker where the target asset expects the event position, such as a weapon or hand attachment point. Check its displayed position against the animated pose rather than only against the rest pose.

A marker and a Projectile_Spawn locator may use related positions, but they are separate data. Moving one does not automatically update the other; save AnimationSet edits and sync locator edits through their respective editors.

For more animation types such as spell casting or ranged attacks, check the Advanced Abilities Guide.

docs.title: 5. Configure Basic Unit Settings
docs.text:
In the upper section of the unit editor, you can configure basic values such as walk speed, run speed, and additional settings for flying units.

Some of these values still need further investigation.

docs.title: 6. Add Audio and Effects
docs.text:
EffectSet is used for sounds and effects. There is a separate Advanced Effects Guide for the full system.

For the basic workflow, it is enough to look at audio for Attack and Spawn.

EffectSet Time also uses a normalized 0..1 range. Match the animation key and variant as well as the time when aligning a sound with a marker. 0.6 means 60% of the selected clip, not 0.6 seconds.

Use the EffectSet editor's Save to persist changes separately from the AnimationSet and locator data. Imported sound references are resource strings; the editor does not automatically package every referenced file or create a game sound bank.

For the exact fields, preview limits, sound types, and reference rules, use the Advanced Effects Guide.

docs.title: 7. Export the Unit
docs.text:
Make the root DRSModel_... collection active and choose File > Export > Battleforge Object/Unit (.drs).

  1. Choose Animated Unit for the unit metadata workflow above, or the matching Animated Object type for an animated prop. Do not export a unit as an animated object if you need its markers, unit effects, and locators.
  2. Enable Export All SKA Actions when you want the clips referenced by the saved AnimationSet written alongside the DRS. It does not mean every Blender action, and an EffectSet-only reference is not enough to select a clip.
  3. Choose Model Name Prefix explicitly. The actual default is No Prefix. Model Name Prefix, Folder Name Prefix, and Keep Existing Prefix serve different naming workflows; verify the resulting names and saved references rather than renaming output files independently.
  4. Leave [DEBUG] Export SKA Tangents enabled for Hermite tangent export unless you deliberately need a stepped/flat debugging comparison. It cannot repair missing keys or an unbaked control rig.
  5. Use the ordinary UV, normal, triangulation, mip-map, and vertex-budget checks from the object guide. Unit collision is not added by populating object collision collections; only collision-enabled animated-object types write that primitive block.

Rig export limitation: The writer exports the deform armature, not an armature whose name contains Control_Rig. It reads deform-bone location/quaternion F-curves and does not automatically bake constraints, IK, or NLA results. A successful control-rig preview is therefore not proof that the exported action contains the same motion. Prepare compatible keyed deform actions on a working copy and verify a fresh SKA import; do not destructively apply transforms or bake away the only copy of your rig.

docs.title: 8. Final Export Result
docs.text: A successful animated export produces the .drs, generated .dds maps, and the referenced .ska clips when action export is enabled. Check the message log and actual files; missing or unresolved action references must not be mistaken for a complete result.

docs.title: Animation round-trip checklist
docs.text:
• The deform armature, skin, and saved AnimationSet refer to the same model and skeleton.
  • Weights were checked across representative poses, with no more than four influences per vertex.
  • AnimationSet and EffectSet edits were saved; locator scene changes were synced.
  • Required action references resolve, and exported filenames match the chosen prefix policy.
  • Marker and sound times were interpreted as normalized fractions.
  • The exported DRS and clips were imported in a separate scene using the same Apply Transform display setting.
  • Animations were checked over their full duration, including looping and bone-attached locators, not just in a still pose.
  • Final behavior was checked in game; preview playback does not prove an external ability or sound resource is configured.

If the mesh is rotated correctly but the animation is not, inspect the deform action, rest pose, and rig/export relationships before changing GO. If a marker or locator appears in Blender but is missing from the export, check the selected model type and the relevant editor's saved metadata.
